Senior Director, Client Experience

About the Role

Market My Market is looking for a Senior Director, Client Experience to own the Client Experience department. Today that department serves more than 320 clients and is made up of two Directors, Client Experience, roughly 11 Client Experience Managers, and 7 Client Success Assistants. This is the leader our two Directors report to, and the person the whole department looks to for direction, standards, and accountability.

This is a leadership seat first. It is built for someone who has already run a client-facing organization inside a fast-growing digital marketing agency, who knows what it takes to keep clients for years, and who can set the tone for how an entire department communicates, inspects its own work, and gets ahead of problems before clients feel them.

You will also keep your feet wet by managing a small portfolio of approximately five accounts of your own, so you are living the same client conversations, reports, and results your team is accountable for. You will own retention, the client messaging standard, and the department's operating rhythm. You will look at the KPIs every week, ask the questions no one else is asking, and teach your directors and their teams to do the same. When something is off, you will propose the fix, not just flag the issue. The Senior Director, Client Experience reports to the CEO and sits on the leadership team.

What You Will Own

Department Leadership & Accountability

  • Lead, coach, and hold accountable Client Experience Managers a team of roughly 11 Client Experience Managers and 7 Client Success Assistants serving 320+ clients. This role will have a handful of direct reports, and will also monitor the success of Client Experience Managers and Client Success Assistants that report to other Directors of Client Experience
  • Set clear expectations and scoreboards for every seat in the department, then inspect against them consistently. Praise in public, correct in private, and never let a miss go unaddressed.
  • Own the department's operating cadence: weekly KPI reviews, portfolio health reviews, one-on-ones, and quarterly rocks that ladder up to company goals.
  • Build the bench. Identify and develop the next generation of CX leaders and make sure every director and manager has a growth plan.
  • Represent Client Experience on the leadership team and partner with the SEO, Content, Paid, Creative, and Business Development leaders so clients experience one company, not five departments.

Client Retention & Portfolio Health

  • Own client retention and lifetime value across every account the department manages. Retention is the number this role is measured on first.
  • Build and run an early-warning system for at-risk clients: know which accounts are drifting before they tell us, and make sure there is a documented save plan and an owner on every one.
  • Personally get involved in the accounts that matter most and the escalations that could cost us a client, then turn what you learn into a repeatable playbook for the team.
  • Drive renewals, upsell, and cross-sell as a natural outcome of well-run accounts, working closely with Business Development.
  • Set the standard for onboarding, the first 90 days, and QBRs so every client understands what we are doing, why, and what it is producing.
  • Manage approximately five client accounts of your own to the same standard you hold the team to, and use that hands-on experience to keep your coaching, playbooks, and expectations grounded in reality.

Messaging & Value Communication

  • Own the messaging standard for the entire department: how we talk about results, how we explain what happened in a month, how we deliver hard news, and how we frame the next recommendation.
  • Build the frameworks, templates, and talk tracks that turn rankings, traffic, calls, and leads into a clear ROI story a practice or business owner cares about.
  • Review client-facing communication, reports, and meeting recaps regularly and coach to the standard. If a client is confused about the value they are getting, that is on us.
  • Make sure every CXM can explain the full MMM offering, including SEO, paid ads, content, web, and Google Business Profile, and position it in a way that fits each client's goals.

KPIs, Inspection & Proactive Operations

  • Define the department's KPIs, including retention, NPS, response time, meeting cadence, upsell, and portfolio health, and report on them to the CEO and leadership team every week.
  • Look at the numbers before anyone asks. Spot the trend, dig into the cause, and show up with a point of view and a recommendation.
  • Teach the team to be proactive, not reactive. Build the habits and checklists that mean clients hear from us with the answer, not the other way around.
  • Audit the work: sit in on client calls, read the reports, review the Asana boards, listen to CallRail calls, and use what you find to raise the bar.
  • Get the most out of the tools we have already invested in, including Zoom Revenue Accelerator, HubSpot, Claude, Replit, and our internal apps, then push them further. Use call intelligence to coach, CRM data to spot risk, and AI to take manual work off the team's plate.
  • Champion automation and AI inside the department so the team spends its time on strategy and relationships instead of manual work, and hold the team to actually adopting what we build.

Solutions & Opportunities

  • Come to the table with solutions. When a process breaks, a client churns, or a report misses the mark, own the root cause and bring a proposed fix with a plan to roll it out.
  • Look for opportunities others miss: new service lines clients are asking for, packaging that would retain better, processes that would free up capacity, and gaps between what we sell and what we deliver.
  • Partner with the SEO Director, Content Director, and PPC Manager on delivery issues that show up in client conversations, and push for fixes that stick.
  • Contribute to case studies, webinars, and thought leadership that show clients and prospects what great looks like.

What Success Looks Like

  • In the first year: Retention is up and churn is predictable, with every at-risk account identified early and worked to a plan.
  • Across the department: Every director and manager knows their numbers, owns their scoreboard, and can explain the story behind it without prompting.

You are comfortable with CRMs (HubSpot preferred), conversation intelligence such as Zoom Revenue Accelerator, AI tools like Claude, low-code platforms like Replit, call tracking, and project management tools, and you use them to inspect and improve rather than just report.

Position Overview

The candidate will work closely with functional teams, business stakeholders, internal audit, and compliance teams to implement effective security controls, minimize access risks, and maintain compliance with organizational policies and audit requirements.

SAP Security & Authorization Development

  • Design, develop, configure, and maintain SAP security roles, composite roles, derived roles, and authorization profiles.

  • Manage user provisioning, role assignments, authorization objects, and access requests across SAP environments.

  • Work with SAP authorization concepts, including PFCG, SU24, SU01, SU53, and ST01, to troubleshoot and resolve authorization issues.

  • Support SAP ECC and/or SAP S/4HANA security, including SAP Fiori applications, catalogs, groups, and authorization roles, as applicable.

  • Perform role modifications, security testing, transport management, and deployment of security changes across development, quality assurance, and production environments.

  • Analyze authorization failures and implement appropriate fixes while following change management procedures.

SAP GRC & Access Control

    • ARM (Access Request Management):Manage and configure access request workflows, approvals, and provisioning processes.

    • EAM (Emergency Access Management):Administer Firefighter access, controller assignments, usage logs, and review processes.

    • BRM (Business Role Management):Support business role definition, role lifecycle management, and governance.

  • Maintain and customize SoD rulesets, risk definitions, functions, and mitigation controls.

  • Perform access risk analysis, role simulations, and remediation of identified security conflicts.

  • Support User Access Reviews (UAR), periodic access certifications, and emergency access reviews.

  • Troubleshoot GRC workflow, integration, provisioning, and authorization issues.

Compliance, Audit & Risk Management

  • Support SOX-related controls, internal audits, external audits, and compliance assessments where applicable.

  • Maintain evidence for access reviews, role approvals, emergency access usage, and security changes.

  • Ensure appropriate segregation between business-critical activities and sensitive transactions.

  • Identify opportunities to strengthen access governance and reduce security risks.

  • Collaborate with auditors and business process owners to resolve findings and implement corrective actions.

Development, Integration & Production Support

  • Analyze security requirements and translate them into technical configurations and development specifications.

  • Support security integration with connected SAP applications and identity or provisioning systems, where applicable.

  • Participate in system upgrades, ERP implementations, security testing, cutover activities, and post-go-live stabilization.

  • Follow ITSM processes for incident, problem, change, and release management.

  • Maintain technical documentation, configuration records, and operational procedures.

Required Technical Skills

  • Strong hands-on experience in SAP Security and SAP GRC Access Control.

  • Experience with SAP GRC Access Control 10.x/12.0 or relevant versions; experience with the client's deployed version is preferred.

  • Strong understanding of SAP role design, authorization objects, profiles, user administration, and role maintenance.

  • Practical experience with PFCG, SU24, SU01, SU53, and authorization troubleshooting.

  • Experience with GRC ARA, ARM, EAM, and BRM.

  • Knowledge of SoD analysis, risk rulesets, mitigation controls, access request workflows, and user access reviews.

  • Experience supporting SAP ECC and/or SAP S/4HANA security.

  • Understanding of SAP transport management, change control, testing, and production deployment processes.

  • Knowledge of audit requirements, security controls, and compliance processes.

  • Strong troubleshooting, analytical, documentation, and stakeholder communication skills.

jobs.title: Analytics Engineer, Finance and Modeling
jobs.excerpt: At In Tandem, we build technology that helps families manage everyday routines and navigate life’s biggest transitions.
jobs.description:
At In Tandem, we build technology that helps families manage everyday routines and navigate life’s biggest transitions. Through our four brands—OurFamilyWizard, Cozi, FamilyWall, and Custody Navigator—we help families stay organized, communicate well, and foster healthy childhoods.
We believe technology should strengthen relationships and make daily coordination less complicated. Everything we create is designed to lighten the mental load, reduce conflict, and support families through big and small moments.
If you want your work to make a real difference in the daily lives of parents and kids, In Tandem is the place where your impact will truly matter.

As an Analytics Engineer (Finance & Modeling), you'll own the metrics, reporting and reconciliation our financial decisions rest on, turning subscription and transaction data across OurFamilyWizard, Cozi, FamilyWall and Custody Navigator into numbers the business can defend. As that foundation becomes automatic, the work shifts toward forecasting and modeling.

You won't start from scratch. Our dbt project is live on Databricks with a star-schema finance mart in production and documented in Unity Catalog. What's missing is the layer on top, and that layer is yours. We also run an internal AI agent that answers business questions in Slack off the semantic layer, so every metric you define and test becomes a question Finance can ask directly rather than queue.

What you'll accomplish:

  • Governed metrics. Add the definitions the finance mart doesn't have yet (ARR, renewal rate, churn, CAC), versioned in dbt and documented in Unity Catalog, with the tests that make each one defensible, and wired into the agent so Finance can ask them directly.
  • Reporting Finance can run without you. Move the recurring finance pack into marimo, retire the Tableau views behind it, and turn a monthly hand-build into something that runs on a schedule.
  • Numbers that reconcile. Reconcile transactions across the app stores, payment processors, subscription systems and the ledger, with automated checks that alert rather than surface at close. Route discrepancies upstream with the evidence attached and turn each one into a test. You build the checks and escalate. Accounting owns the treatment.
  • Forecasting for Finance. Cohort subscriber and revenue projection, and aggregate renewal and retention forecasting, feeding the CFO's forecast and board reporting. LTV by acquisition source, feeding paid spend allocation with Growth. Pricing and promo impact, modeled before we ship rather than measured after. Individual churn propensity and uplift follow once there's a retention motion ready to act on the scores.
  • Models ship as scored tables in dbt and Unity Catalog, with tests, lineage and a definition the agent can answer from. Not as notebooks.

Who you are:

  • Statistically rigorous. You know why a cohort curve is the wrong shape, what a model is leaking, and when a result is noise.
  • Fluent in finance, and unwilling to let a number you can't explain go out the door. When two systems disagree, you find out why and tell the people upstream.
  • An engineer who owns the number end to end, from a CFO's question through the model, the test, the report and the conversation that follows. A spreadsheet nobody can reproduce reads to you as a liability.
  • AI-proficient in practice, not in theory. Claude Code, coding agents and agent SDKs are part of our daily loop, and we expect you to already work this way. A lot of what used to be a week of modeling work is now an afternoon, and we're hiring for people who have internalized that.
  • Willing to wear several hats. This is a small team supporting four brands. Some weeks you're deep in a retention model, some weeks you're chasing an app store discrepancy or unblocking someone else's dashboard. The scope above is the center of the role, not a fence around it.
  • Motivated by work that matters. Families rely on these products during real moments in their lives.

What you bring:

  • 3+ years in analytics engineering, data science, BI engineering or advanced analytics.
  • Statistical modeling shipped into a business process: forecasting, survival or cohort analysis, or propensity.
  • Measuring the lift from a price change or a growth experiment. You don't need to have designed the test, but you need to be able to read the result honestly and say what it's worth.
  • Subscription metrics you've built and defended to a finance stakeholder: ARR/MRR, renewal, churn, LTV/CAC, or cohort revenue.
  • Strong SQL and real dimensional modeling. You've designed marts, not just queried them.
  • Python and Git as daily habits.
Nice to have, not a dealbreaker:
  • dbt, Databricks and Unity Catalog, or a comparable lakehouse.
  • Reconciling transactional data to a financial system of record.
  • Code-first notebook reporting (marimo, Hex, Streamlit, Quarto).

ROLE DETAILS

JOB TITLE

Chief of Staff

Full Time

Role overview

About the client

The client is a dynamic multi-entity family office and serial entrepreneur operating across four distinct market sectors:

  1. Real Estate Investment & Development: A portfolio of cash-investment residential properties across multiple regions, managed under individual entity structures alongside property management for outside owners.
  2. Boutique Interior Design & Contracting: A boutique interior design practice specializing in high-end residential projects, turnkey furnishing, and property contracting.
  3. Boutique Fitness & Wellness: A fast-growing infrared fitness studio brand with locations across key markets undergoing strategic expansion, corporate structuring, and location rollouts.
  4. Personal & Family Office: Family office administration, executive scheduling, and personal household logistics.

The business operates with a small, high-touch core team—including licensed brokers, property accountants, bookkeepers, and studio managers. The Managing Partner requires a central partner to maintain cross-business oversight, streamline administrative follow-through, and bridge operational gaps across all four sectors.

About the role

As the Chief of Staff, you will serve as the primary point of organizational accountability and central connective tissue across all four business entities and personal operations.

You are the "layer above and between" the Managing Partner, external accountants, bookkeepers, studio managers, contractors, and clients—ensuring information is gathered, organized, updated, and dispatches to the right people on time. You will manage executive priorities, oversee property management logistics, support back-office design procurement, monitor fitness expansion deliverables, and handle high-level executive and personal administration.

As you demonstrate capability, the role will expand to include light marketing, client outreach, and broader operational management to drive business growth and client retention.



BUSINESS AREA

HOURS ALLOCATION

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES & SCOPE

1. Real Estate & Property

Baseline: 10 hrs/wk

Swing: 6–16 hrs

  • Master Property Registry maintenance
  • Monthly utility close & statement reviews
  • Tenant/vendor communications & access
  • Turnover SOPs & lease renewals

2. Design & Contracting

Baseline: 10 hrs/wk

Swing: 6–14 hrs

  • Project back-office & budget tracking
  • Purchasing, orders & trade logistics
  • Client invoicing & vendor matching
  • CRM marketing & portfolio updates

3. Fitness Brand

Baseline: 10 hrs/wk

Swing: 6–14 hrs

  • Investment & reimbursement tracking
  • Corporate entity & lease compliance
  • Build-out & expansion tracking
  • Agency & marketing follow-through

4. Executive & Family Admin

Baseline: 10 hrs/wk

Swing: 6–12 hrs

  • Calendar triage & focus protection
  • Family appointments & logistics
  • Travel itineraries & household admin

Key responsibilities

1. Real Estate Investment & Property Management Coordination

  • Master Property Registry: Maintain a current master database across all properties (holding entities, tenant details, rent schedules, security deposit holdings, lease expiration alerts at 120/90/60 days, insurance policies, tax appeal timelines, and utility logins).
  • Monthly Utility Close: Download, review, flag variance (>20% spikes), and reconcile monthly statements across all owner-paid utilities by the 7th of every month for the bookkeeper.
  • Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs): Write and execute SOPs for acquisitions, tenant move-in/move-out workflows, utility transfers, lease renewals, and maintenance requests.
  • Property Administration: Field tenant and vendor requests, coordinate property access, manage insurance/permit renewals, and log property maintenance/markup fees.

2. Boutique Interior Design Practice Support

  • Project Back-Office: Set up and maintain project files, scope sheets, vendor contracts, and decision logs for all active interior design jobs.
  • Purchasing & Logistics Tracker: Track all orders from procurement to delivery (SKUs, deposits, delivery dates, damage reports, and storage logistics).
  • Budget & Invoicing Control: Perform weekly updates on budget vs. committed spend; draft client invoices, reconcile vendor receipts, and pass coded records to the financial team.
  • Marketing & Client Outreach: Compile project photos, maintain the CRM database, draft client check-ins, coordinate project photography, and manage digital portfolio updates during lull periods.

3. Fitness & Wellness Business Operations Support

  • Investment & Capital Tracking: Maintain a clear ledger of capital contributions, member loans, and business expenses; ensure all brand-related spend is executed on dedicated business cards.
  • Corporate & Compliance Records: Track studio LLC entities, lease terms/options, insurance renewals, and legal agreements.
  • Expansion & Build-Out Logistics: Maintain project timelines, site evaluation files, contractor schedules, and grand-opening checklists for new studio locations.
  • Agency & Marketing Follow-Up: Monitor external marketing, PR, and ad agencies against agreed deliverables, timelines, and scope.

4. Executive & Personal Administration

  • Calendar Management: Triage, structure, and protect the Managing Partner’s calendar; confirm daily appointments, resolve conflicts proactive of client meetings, and block focus time.
  • Family Logistics & Personal Admin: Coordinate recurring family appointments, school calendars, travel itineraries, household vendors, and personal renewals with absolute discretion.
  • Inbox & Triage Management: Monitor primary inboxes, flag priority action items, and draft responses to maintain timely follow-up.

Operating Cadence & AI Tooling

  • Daily Morning Brief: Deliver a daily summary detailing priorities, required approvals, and daily schedules before Eastern business hours begin.
  • Daily Close-Out Note: Provide an end-of-shift update on completed tasks and pending items.
  • Weekly Syncs: Conduct a weekly strategy review with the Managing Partner and structured handoffs with the financial team.
  • AI-Enabled Execution: Utilize modern AI productivity tools (such as Claude/Claude Design) to quickly generate project spec sheets, floor plans, draft communications, summarize documents, and prepare client-facing materials.

Qualifications & skills (Non-Negotiable)

  • 5+ Years Experience: Proven track record in a high-level support role—such as Chief of Staff, Operations Manager, or Senior Executive Assistant—directly supporting a Founder or Senior Executive across multiple business entities.
  • Real Estate / Property Management Background: Direct experience handling property back-office operations, leases, utility setups, tenant transitions, and vendor coordination.
  • Financial & Numerical Aptitude: Proficient in spreadsheet management, budget tracking, invoice reconciliation, and preparing clean reporting packages for bookkeepers/accountants.
  • Systems Builder Mindset: Proven ability to create, implement, and maintain SOPs, CRM databases, project trackers, and checklists independently.
  • AI & Tech Proficiency: Comfortable utilizing modern software and AI tools (Claude/Claude Design, CRM platforms, project management tools, shared password managers) to drive operational efficiency.
  • Communication Skills: Flawless written and verbal English communication skills with a professional, warm, and collaborative tone suitable for high-touch clients and external partners.
  • Proven Tenure: Demonstrated history of long-term reliability and stability in previous positions.
  • Availability & Reliability: Available full-time (40 hours/week) during US Eastern business hours, with a reliable remote work setup (including backup power/internet solutions where applicable).

Qualifications & skills (Non-Negotiable)

  • Spanish language proficiency is a plus.
  • Prior familiarity with property tracking tools, password manager security vaults, and modern financial reporting tools (e.g., Ramp, QuickBooks read-access).

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • 100% On-Time Monthly Financial Packages: Utility closes, invoices, and expense logs delivered cleanly to the financial team by designated monthly deadlines.
  • Zero Lapsed Obligations: Zero missed lease renewal deadlines, insurance renewals, or permit expirations.
  • Seamless Transitions: Zero gaps in utility service during property turnover events.
  • Budget Accuracy: Design and expansion budgets updated weekly with proactive flags on budget variances.
  • Operational Autonomy: Founder’s direct administrative workload demonstrably reduced within the first 90 days.

Everything we produce is aimed at one thing: making it easier for customer-facing teams to tell a differentiated Kobie story.

As a Sr. Sales Enablement Associate, you will work in two modes. Reactively, you will support active deals by producing sales artifacts on demand, from RFP responses to pitch content to demo support, always in partnership with Business Development, who own the win. Proactively, you will build the enablement engine itself: playbooks, battlecards, training, and the content library that keeps it all organized and current. This role reports into Kobie's GTM Enablement team and has no direct reports. It is a hands-on execution role for someone with strong systems thinking who believes in progress over perfection, leaves every asset better than they found it, and wants to grow their impact as the function scales.

How you will make an impact

  • Produce deal-driven sales artifacts on demand, including RFP and RFI responses in Loopio, pitch deck story sections in PowerPoint, and demo or vignette support, executed to Kobie's bar of excellence in partnership with Business Development, who are accountable for winning the deal.
  • Draft and tailor objection-handling guides, talk tracks, and decision trees that equip Business Development and Client Services to position Kobie confidently in live selling situations.
  • Build and maintain sales playbooks, battlecards, and positioning materials that guide how teams message and sell Kobie products across the loyalty and martech landscape.
  • Produce sales training content and enablement videos in Synthesia, giving Business Development and Client Services repeatable, self-serve resources they can return to.
  • Maintain the RFP response repository in Loopio, keeping answer libraries current, accurate, and easy to retrieve so turnaround gets faster over time.
  • Apply Claude and other AI tools to accelerate drafting, summarize competitive and market inputs, and increase both the volume and the quality of enablement output.
  • Compile competitive intelligence on loyalty and martech vendors, including competitors such as Salesforce, Capillary, and IBS, and translate it into positioning teams can use.
  • Maintain accurate enablement and content records in HubSpot so the team can see which assets support which deals and what is actually being used.
  • Organize and version-control a single source of truth for sales content, applying consistent structure so teammates always find the current, correct asset.
  • Track usage and feedback on playbooks, materials, and tools, and implement improvements so the highest-value assets stay sharp and low-value ones get retired.
  • Contribute market and competitive insights surfaced through deal work back to GTM Enablement and Product, helping shape what we build and how we position it.
  • Turn around deal-support requests quickly and reliably, becoming the trusted first call for Business Development when a deadline is tight.
  • Leave every asset better than you found it, tightening messaging, closing gaps, and improving structure with each pass rather than waiting for a full rebuild.
  • At the end of the first year, success would mean a well-organized and actively used content library, faster RFx and pitch turnaround, and a battlecard and playbook set that Business Development reaches for without being asked.

What you need to be successful

    Required

  • 2 to 4 years of experience in sales enablement, GTM enablement, competitive intelligence, or a related content and sales-support function.
  • Builds and maintains RFP and RFI responses in Loopio, including answer library upkeep and full response assembly under deadline.
  • Produces polished, on-brand sales and training decks in PowerPoint, translating complex solutions into clear, client-ready narratives, working to direct agency services for final polish as needed.
  • Creates enablement and training videos in Synthesia, or a comparable platform, to deliver repeatable, self-serve learning content.
  • Applies Claude and other AI tools to draft, summarize, and accelerate enablement content, with sound judgment on accuracy and brand fit.
  • Maintains sales and content data in HubSpot, keeping records accurate and retrievable to support pipeline-facing work.
  • Builds sales playbooks, battlecards, and objection-handling guides that hold up in live selling situations.
  • Compiles and maintains competitive intelligence on loyalty and martech vendors, translating findings into positioning teams can act on.
  • Organizes and version-controls a shared content library so teams reliably find the current, correct asset.
  • Familiarity with SaaS, CRM, and loyalty or martech concepts sufficient to position Kobie accurately in market.

    • Strongly Preferred

  • Prior sales, pre-sales, or business development experience that informs how enablement lands inside a live deal. Sales storytelling and narrative building around product materials is ideal.
  • Experience leveraging AI as a workflow enhancer (not a substitute for judgment/thinking). Ideal candidate would have experience building repeatable AI-assisted workflows.
  • Demonstrated ability to pick up and manage new tools quickly, applying strong systems thinking to how content and tools fit together (Experience with Hubspot, Notion, HighSpot, and similar CRM/Sales tools preferred).
  • Familiarity with building win/loss synthesis and decision-tree logic to sharpen future materials.
  • Familiarity with the loyalty marketing and martech competitive landscape, including vendors such as Salesforce, Capillary, and Epsilon.
Who we are As a trusted partner, Kobie delivers market-leading, end-to-end loyalty solutions designed to enable customer experiences for the world's most successful brands. We do this with a strategy-led technology approach that uncovers the truth behind what drives consumers on an emotional level. We believe that our team's passion and expertise are the driving forces behind our success and are proud to be named a Top Workplaces in the USA, where the best and brightest in loyalty drive our mission of growing enterprise value through loyalty.
A place for all We celebrate and embrace diversity at Kobie!
Employment at Kobie is based solely on an individual's merit and qualifications, which are directly related to professional competence. We do not discriminate against any teammate or applicant because of race,color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, national origin, disability, age, genetic information, veteran status, marital status, pregnancy, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.
We are fiercely committed to fostering a workplace where teammates can bring their authentic selves to work every day. Our DEI initiatives, including various committees, ensure that principles of equity, diversity, and inclusion are deeply ingrained throughout Kobie. While our leadership team fully supports our policy of nondiscrimination and equal opportunity, it is the responsibility of all teammates to uphold these values.
Ready to join us? If you’re ready to make an impact and grow in a supportive, innovative environment, we’d love to hear from you. Apply today and join the best and brightest in loyalty!

Who We Are

Insurity empowers insurance organizations to quickly capitalize on new opportunities by delivering the world’s most configurable, cloud-native, easy-to-use, and intuitively analytical insurance software. Just as importantly, we empower our people—providing the tools, support, and opportunities they need to grow and succeed.

We don’t just make bold promises—we deliver results. As the largest cloud-based software provider for the Property & Casualty market, Insurity is trusted by 22 of the top 25 P&C carriers and 7 of the top 10 wholesale brokers in the MGA space. Behind that trust is a team that delivers exceptional value and deep industry expertise.

While our technology sets us apart, it’s our people who truly make the difference. At Insurity, you’ll collaborate with some of the most creative and knowledgeable minds in insurance tech—in a culture that fosters innovation, teamwork, and continuous learning. Our award-winning onboarding experience welcomes and supports you from the moment you accept our offer.

Ready to grow your career with an industry leader? Apply today—we’re excited to welcome you. #UatInsurity

Insurity’s NextPartner Success Manager

We are looking for our next Partner Success Manager to help us manage our growing ecosystem of System Integrator and Technology Partners. You will be a critical cog in the gears that drive mutual revenue growth for both Insurity and your assigned ecosystem Partners.

 What Our Partner Success Manager Will Do

The Partner Success Manager is responsible for the day-to-day management and operations of the Insurity Partner Program (IPP), launched in January 2026, and their assigned Partners. This role oversees onboarding and ongoing management of Partners, supports Partner operational requirements across their lifecycle, and helps design and execute/drive Partner-led GTM efforts to build qualified joint pipeline and drive incremental revenue for Insurity and our Partners. The Partner Success Manager also collaborates with Program leadership to design, implement, and refine AI automation processes that improve operational efficiency, velocity, and throughput.

Responsibilities will include the following for your assigned/named Partners:

Relationship Management

• Serve as the primary operational point of contact for assigned Partners throughout their lifecycle.
• Manage inbound Partner requests from initial engagement through exit, as needed.
• Perform due diligence on new Partner signup requests, present the Program, support joint GTM business plans, onboard partners and their resources into our systems, and help execute agreed tactical initiatives.
• Proactively communicate resources, training, product materials, marketing assets, Portal guidance, and QBR/EBR coordination needed for Partner success.
• Support Partner renewal processes and help execute structured Partner exit processes when required.
• Manage Partner communications such as newsletters and event invitations in partnership with Partner Marketing and Product.
• Manage Partner sponsorships of Insurity events and drive Partner Day attendance/sponsorship package sales with assigned Partners. Participate at Partner Day as deemed appropriate by Management.

Program Operations & Delivery

• Orchestrate Partner onboarding by creating Partner and contact records in SFDC PRM, assigning training, and ensuring required systems, environments, and tools are in place.
• Ensure accuracy and completeness of lead forecasting, deal registration, opportunity tagging, and related SFDC CRM/PRM updates for assigned Partners.
• Manage deal registration and assigned Partner sales pipeline processes, including overlap checks against direct sales, existing Partner submissions, and the current Insurity client base.
• Manage Partner legal agreement processing and coordinate with the appropriate internal stakeholders.
• Own Partner Sales Assist Fee (SAF) / referral fee calculations and payment tracking in partnership with Finance.
• Coordinate Program operations that support joint Partner marketing and sales activities, including campaigns, events, Campaign-in-a-Box, and Deal-in-a-Box initiatives.
• Lead Partner performance monitoring and reporting for assigned Partners, including annual promotion / relegation reviews within the Partner tiering model.

Internal Process

• Manage operational interactions within the PRM Partner Portal for assigned Partners, including operational “how do I...?” support.
• Create and maintain Program documentation such as Partner agreements, Program guidelines, GTM sales kits, and enablement assets.
• Track and analyze operational and performance metrics to identify trends, issues, and opportunities to improve Program effectiveness.
• Develop and implement approved automation and agentic AI-driven process improvements that streamline Partner Program operations.
• Drive continuous improvements in the overall Insurity Partner experience and Partner Program operations.
• Help design and launch our Operations AI Fleet of agents to automate many partner tasks for improved partner experiences.

• Other related duties as assigned

Who We’re Looking For 

  • 5–7 years of relevant business experience in enterprise SaaS Partner Success Management or a closely related role.
  • Bachelor’s degree in a related field (equivalent work experience may be considered).
  • Strong understanding of the Insurity Partner Program, Partner lifecycle management, and Partner-led GTM motions.
  • Working knowledge of Insurity products, SaaS / BaaS positioning, and how Partners generate qualified pipeline and revenue.
  • Familiarity with Partner scorecards, tiering models, incentive programs, and co-sell / referral processes.
  • Working knowledge of enterprise software operations; insurance / P&C market familiarity preferred.
  • Have the ability to perform these skills at an advanced level:
    • Ability to create concise, audience-relevant, objective-oriented documentation and communications.

    • Analytical and critical thinking.

    • Written and oral English communication.
    • Time management including work planning, prioritization, and organization.
    • Ability to handle multiple priorities or tasks.
    • Self-starter and quick learner.
    • Detail-oriented and process disciplined.
    • Active listening and cross-functional collaboration.
    • Expectation management.
    • Project management.
    • Process analysis, design, and management.
    • Data analysis and metric interpretation.
    • Business acumen and Partner Program acumen.
    • Technical acumen across SaaS systems and workflows.
    • Change management.
    • Coaching, training, and Partner enablement.
    • Meeting facilitation and professional presentation of information.
    • Partner advocacy.

  • Nice to have: complete one or more of the following:
    • Applicable insurance certification(s).
    • Salesforce / SFDC PRM-related certification(s).
    • Partner ecosystem / channel program certification(s).
  • Advanced experience & knowledge:
    • SFDC CRM and SFDC PRM.
    • PRM Partner Portal administration and support workflows.
    • Lead registration, opportunity management, and pipeline hygiene processes.
    • Workflow, ticketing, and project management tools.
    • Reporting, spreadsheet, and dashboard tools.
    • Document, knowledge-management, and enablement repositories.
    • Automation and agentic AI tools used to improve Partner operations.
  • Travel required 0-20%

What’s In It For U 

Work Where You Thrive
Find the work environment that supports your best—whether that’s remote, in-office, or hybrid—depending on your role and location. Our Flex First Workforce approach offers many fully remote opportunities, while some teams follow hybrid or in-office schedules to stay connected and collaborative.

Take Time When You Need It
We trust our team to manage their time with our Open PTO Policy, empowering you to recharge when it matters most.

Benefits That Start on Day One
Enjoy comprehensive health coverage and employer-matched retirement savings right from your first day—because we know how important these are to you.

Living Our Values Every Day
Our core values are more than words on a wall—they guide how we hire, grow, and retain the very best talent.

Award-Winning Onboarding
From your first day to your first anniversary, our onboarding program is designed to set you up for success and help you make an immediate impact.

Grow Your Career from Within
We believe in promoting from within. In fact, over 25% of our open roles are filled by internal candidates.

Mentorship That Matters
Our mentorship program connects you with experienced leaders who are committed to helping you grow both personally and professionally.

Insurity Podcasts
Explore podcasts from our Learning & Development team for deeper insight into Insurity products, company innovation, and the business as a whole.

Keep Learning, Always
Fuel your growth with full access to LinkedIn Learning and Kaplan—because continuous development is key to success.

Invest in Your Future—And Your Family’s
Through our partnership with the University of Arizona Global Campus, you and your family can access discounted tuition and pursue educational goals affordably.

Earn When You Refer
Love where you work? Invite others to join us! Our Employee Referral Bonus program rewards you for bringing great people on board.

We have five Core Values at Insurity; one of which is to Act with Integrity.  Providing pay transparency helps you make the best decision for you.  We continuously analyze and update our salary ranges for our roles according to market trends to not only ensure our employees are paid fairly, but also help close gender, race, and disability wage gaps. Along with the benefits listed above, the career level salary range for this role is $70,000 to $140,000. We share a career level salary as a guideline; however, actual salary may vary based on your experience and qualifications. If your application advances, your recruiter will review these details with you during a video interview.

Insurity is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer 

We are dedicated to creating an exceptional work environment for all our employees by extending a culture of diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging into the very fabric of our organization.  We embrace differences and diversity of identity, experience, and thought, and actively strive for inclusive behaviors across our company. 

 We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application and/or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment.  Please contact us to request accommodation. 

Thank you for your interest in Insurity!  Please understand that due to the volume of applicants we receive, only selected candidates will be contacted. 

   #innovateatinsurity

If you are a California resident, the California Consumer Privacy Act (“CCPA”), as amended by the California Privacy Rights Act (“CPRA”), requires us to provide you with information regarding how we collect, use, and disclose your personal information in connection with your application for employment.

Insurity may share your personal information with service providers, affiliates, and authorized third parties involved in recruiting, hiring, onboarding, information technology, security, and compliance activities, as permitted by applicable law.

jobs.description:
Who We Are

At Partnerize, we're on a mission to transform the way businesses grow. We've built the leading partnership automation platform that empowers brands to discover, engage, and convert their audiences at scale. From affiliate marketing to influencer collaborations, we help our clients build and manage profitable partnerships that drive real results. We're a team of passionate problem-solvers who are dedicated to helping our clients win in the ever-evolving world of digital marketing.

Why Join Us

We're looking for passionate, talented people who want to be part of a winning team. At Partnerize, you'll find a culture of collaboration, innovation, and respect. We're guided by our core values, and we're committed to creating an environment where everyone can do their best work. We also offer a competitive salary, generous benefits, and a flexible work environment that allows you to thrive both personally and professionally. If you're ready to grow your career and make a difference, we'd love to hear from you.

Job Summary

Please note: This is an Individual Contributor (IC) role with no people management responsibilities. You will own the full enterprise sales cycle—from prospecting through to close—building your own pipeline and driving net-new enterprise revenue.

The Senior Enterprise Account Executive is responsible for identifying, qualifying and closing net-new enterprise opportunities within our highest-potential target accounts. As the digital marketing landscape continues to evolve, you'll help enterprise brands navigate increasingly complex partnership and performance marketing strategies to deliver measurable commercial outcomes.

You'll become a trusted advisor to senior marketing leaders, building consultative relationships, uncovering strategic business challenges and demonstrating how Partnerize's technology creates long-term value. We're looking for a proactive hunter and accomplished enterprise seller who thrives on generating pipeline, managing complex sales cycles and consistently exceeding revenue targets.

Responsibilities

  • Build & Own Your Pipeline: Proactively generate new enterprise opportunities using AI-powered sales tools, intent data, outbound prospecting and strategic account planning.
  • Lead Consultative Discovery: Conduct high-impact discovery conversations with senior marketing stakeholders to uncover business challenges and position Partnerize's solutions against measurable commercial outcomes.
  • Develop Commercial Business Cases: Build compelling value propositions and ROI-driven business cases that demonstrate revenue growth, operational efficiency and long-term business value.
  • Manage Complex Enterprise Sales Cycles: Navigate multi-stakeholder buying processes across marketing, procurement, legal, security and finance to progress opportunities from discovery through to close.
  • Forecast with Accuracy: Maintain accurate CRM data, manage pipeline health and deliver reliable sales forecasting through disciplined opportunity management.
  • Deliver Executive-Level Presentations: Tailor presentations and product demonstrations that clearly communicate Partnerize's value proposition and differentiate our platform within the partnership ecosystem.
  • Achieve Revenue Targets: Consistently meet or exceed quarterly and annual sales targets while maintaining a high level of customer engagement and pipeline activity.

Required Qualifications & Competencies

  • Enterprise Sales Experience: Up to five years of quota-carrying experience selling enterprise SaaS, MarTech, digital media or technology solutions into mid-market and enterprise organisations.
  • Individual Contributor Mindset: A highly motivated self-starter who enjoys building pipeline from scratch and thrives in a high-autonomy, high-performance sales environment.
  • Consultative Selling Expertise: Experience applying value-based sales methodologies such as MEDDPICC, Challenger or similar frameworks to manage complex enterprise sales cycles.
  • Executive Presence: Strong commercial acumen with the confidence to influence and challenge senior decision-makers through consultative conversations.
  • AI & Sales Technology: Comfortable leveraging AI-powered sales tools, CRM platforms, sales engagement technologies and intent data to improve prospecting, research and pipeline management.
  • Ecommerce & Digital Marketing Knowledge: An understanding of ecommerce, affiliate marketing, partnerships or the wider digital marketing landscape. Direct affiliate marketing experience is advantageous but not essential.
  • Modern Marketing Fluency: Strong understanding of today's performance marketing ecosystem, including affiliate marketing, creator partnerships and ecommerce.
  • Highly Autonomous & Driven: Exceptionally organised, resilient and self-motivated, with the discipline to manage a high-volume outbound sales cadence while working remotely.

Desired Qualifications & Competencies

  • Experience selling MarTech, affiliate marketing or partnership technology solutions.
  • Experience working within a high-growth enterprise SaaS organisation.
  • Proven success selling into retail, ecommerce or D2C brands.
  • Experience managing complex enterprise sales cycles involving multiple stakeholders.
  • Familiarity with Salesforce or similar CRM platforms and modern sales engagement tools.

US Benefits & Perks

  • Flexible Time Off Policy – Take the time you need.
  • Enhanced Parental Leave: 16 weeks for birth parents and 8 weeks for non-birth parents at full pay after one year of employment.
  • Robust company-sponsored Health & Welfare Benefits.
  • 401(k) Plan with a 4% company match.
  • Enhanced Wellness Programme, including access to an Employee Assistance Programme (EAP), Wellness Coaching and Wellness Fridays.
  • Regular company events and activities.

Compensation Range

USD $150,000–$180,000 base salary + commission package

Our salary range is intended to cover roles across the United States. An individual's base salary will be determined based on factors including geographic location, relevant experience, skills, knowledge and overall qualifications.

Our Commitment to Diversity & Inclusion

We are committed to attracting, developing, and advancing our outstanding team members, regardless of race, ethnic identity, sexual orientation, religion, age, gender, gender identity, physical abilities, or any other dimension of diversity. We strive to foster an environment where people can be their authentic selves, raise concerns and innovate, all without fear; where they are treated fairly and respectfully, have equal access to opportunities and resources and can contribute fully to the organization’s success. Every individual in our business is expected to live this commitment without exception.

jobs.description:
Req ID:394104

NTT DATA strives to hire exceptional, innovative and passionate individuals who want to grow with us. If you want to be part of an inclusive, adaptable, and forward-thinking organization, apply now.

We are currently seeking a Senior Production Support Engineer/Salesforce Admin - Remote Canada Position to join our team in Toronto, Ontario (CA-ON), Canada (CA).

Reporting to the IT Team Lead, the Senior Production Support Engineer will be a key member of the Platform Production Support team, responsible for ensuring the stability, availability, performance, and reliability of business-critical applications and integrations.

This role will provide Level 2 / Level 3 production support, troubleshoot complex application and integration issues, perform root cause analysis, coordinate incident resolution, and implement preventive and corrective actions. The position requires strong hands-on technical expertise along with a solid understanding of production support processes, incident management, change management, monitoring, and operational excellence.

The Senior Production Support Engineer will work closely with application development teams, infrastructure teams, integration teams, business stakeholders, and third-party vendors to maintain reliable services and ensure production issues are resolved within agreed service levels.

Primary Duties and Responsibilities

  • Provide Level 2 / Level 3 production support for Applications including Salesforce applications, integrations, interfaces, batch processes, and associated services.
  • Monitor production environments and proactively identify application, integration, performance, and data-related issues.
  • Troubleshoot and resolve production incidents involving Apex, Lightning components, Visualforce, workflows, flows, validation rules, integrations, APIs, security, and data.
  • Perform detailed incident analysis and drive timely restoration of services in accordance with defined SLAs.
  • Participate in Major Incident Management and collaborate with cross-functional teams during high-priority production incidents.
  • Perform Root Cause Analysis (RCA) for recurring and high-impact incidents and identify corrective and preventive actions.
  • Analyze application logs, debug logs, integration failures, API errors, batch failures, and system exceptions to determine root causes.
  • Support integrations with third-party applications using REST/SOAP APIs, middleware, batch interfaces, and other integration mechanisms.
  • Monitor scheduled jobs, batch Apex processes, integration jobs, queues, and other critical production processes.
  • Perform controlled production fixes and minor code/configuration changes where required to restore or improve service.
  • Work with development teams to coordinate permanent fixes for defects identified through production incidents.
  • Participate in release validation, deployment support, smoke testing, and post-production implementation verification.
  • Support change management activities and ensure production changes follow established governance and approval processes.
  • Maintain and enhance operational documentation including Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), Knowledge Articles, troubleshooting guides, support playbooks, and recovery procedures.
  • Identify recurring incidents and opportunities for automation, monitoring improvements, and operational efficiencies.
  • Ensure production systems meet required standards for reliability, availability, auditability, scalability, security, and operational supportability.
  • Participate in on-call and after-hours production support as required for critical incidents, releases, and scheduled maintenance.
  • Support service management processes including Incident Management, Problem Management, Change Management, Knowledge Management, and Service Request Management.
  • Track production support metrics and contribute to service improvement initiatives focused on incident reduction, system stability, and SLA performance.
  • Perform other responsibilities as requested by the Manager or Team Lead.

Knowledge Skills & Abilities

  • Strong hands-on knowledge of platforms with extensive production support and troubleshooting experience.
  • Strong understanding of Apex, Lightning, Visualforce, SOQL/SOSL, Salesforce Flows, validation rules, triggers, workflows, and platform configuration.
  • Experience supporting applications integrated with relational database management systems and enterprise applications.
  • Experience with mass data handling and integration tools such as Informatica, MuleSoft, Data Loader, or similar technologies is preferred.
  • Strong understanding of production support processes including Incident Management, Problem Management, Change Management, and Root Cause Analysis.
  • Familiarity with ITIL-based service management processes is highly desirable.
  • Experience working with ITSM platforms such as ServiceNow or similar tools is preferred.
  • Ability to troubleshoot complex issues across multiple systems and identify dependencies between upstream/downstream applications.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to quickly diagnose critical production issues.
  • Ability to prioritize multiple production incidents and service requests in a high-volume support environment.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to communicate technical issues clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently as well as collaboratively across application, infrastructure, vendor, and business teams.
  • Ability to identify recurring operational problems and recommend automation or permanent corrective solutions.
  • Strong focus on service reliability, customer experience, and continuous improvement.

Required Qualifications.

  • 5+ years experience, with significant experience supporting enterprise applications.

SALARY RANGE: $166,000-185,000

Sightline Institute is hiring a Principal Director, Program Development, to build our next research program, and then the one after that. This position is new, created to identify and launch new research areas. The Principal Director scouts, vets, and recommends each new program area. Then they launch it: conducting and publishing the original research that establishes Sightline’s credibility in the field, developing the strategy, anchoring early fundraising, and helping recruit the program’s permanent director. Once that director is in place, the Principal Director begins again with the next area, in a recurring three- to five-year cycle. The handoff is by design. The goal is a new program that stands on its own, led by someone hired to carry it forward, so the Principal Director can start the next one. The Principal Director is an accomplished researcher, a skilled writer and speaker, and an experienced program builder. Because the subject changes every few years, we are less interested in deep expertise in any one field than in range. You would be joining an organization of experienced staff members, fully remote across Cascadia. New programs have always come out of our team of researchers and communicators, kicking ideas around until someone finds the angle. We are more a guild of artisans than a factory, and this role is also built to work that way: you would be working in collaboration with colleagues who know the region and its politics well. This full-time, salaried role reports to the Executive Director and works in close partnership with Sightline’s senior staff. This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to a respected organization with an established track record of success while ushering in expanded areas of impact and reach. This is a unique, dynamic position that will directly contribute to Sightline’s impact and to creating strong communities, a green economy and a healthy environment throughout Cascadia.

About Sightline Institute

Our mission is to make Cascadia, the region stretching from Alaska to northern California and the Pacific to the Rocky Mountain States, a global model of sustainability— with strong communities, a green economy, and a healthy environment. Founded in 1993, Sightline is one of the region’s most influential public policy think tanks. In 2026 alone, we helped pass six housing laws in Idaho, four in Washington, and two in Oregon, along with Missoula’s new zoning code and a major clean energy law in Washington. Several of these were US firsts. Our work on election reform has helped shape how Alaska, Portland, and Seattle run their elections.

In our programs on climate and energy, housing and cities, and democracy and elections, we identify and promote reforms that yield outsized improvements for the region’s people and places. A nonprofit, nonpartisan, and independent public policy research center, Sightline provides research, articles, and commentary; maps, graphics, and tools; and framing and messaging guidance. Sightline’s influence depends on the depth and breadth of our researchers’ expertise and their persuasiveness in presenting analysis and arguments. We aim to draw attention to and build support for data-backed solutions to specific public problems through close engagement in policy debates. We advise and inform public officials, advocates, and the media. We also help organize unusual coalitions, advocate to leaders, and lobby lawmakers, usually at the state level.

Our combination of deep expertise; trusted resources for leaders, advocates, and journalists; practical, research-based policy recommendations; powerful case making and persuasive argumentation; and strategic engagement in unusual coalitions have made Sightline extremely effective at advancing progress toward our mission.

Learn more at .

Why now?

Sightline has been doing this work in Cascadia for 33 years. We have grown steadily, doubling in budget over the past decade and accumulating financial reserves that provide us with stability and options. Generously supported by families and charitable foundations from Cascadia and beyond, we are in the strongest financial position of our history, with a seasoned staff and systems built to support a larger team.

Even so, our region has 21 million people and we have 21 staff. Gradual growth has been good for our culture and our effectiveness, but at this pace, we will never make Cascadia the global model of sustainability we exist to build. So we are trying something different: rather than growing new programs slowly from within, as we always have, we are hiring someone to build them.

Essential Responsibilities

  • Scouts, plans, and builds new research programs for Sightline, developing and refining an institutional system for expanding into new issue areas
  • Vets potential program areas against Sightline’s program-selection criteria and leads a selection process that draws on input from across the organization, recommending a new program area for the Executive Director’s decision
  • Conducts preliminary research and produces ground-breaking articles and analyses that establish Sightline’s presence and reputation in each new issue area
  • Plans a maximally impactful strategy for each new program that draws on Sightline’s strengths in research, communications, and coalition building, and begins stitching together a coalition in support of it
  • Serves as a senior spokesperson for Sightline; writes and publishes research, speaks publicly and to the media, and meets with policymakers, allies, and other stakeholders
  • Anchors fundraising for each new program, working with the development team to identify, cultivate, and secure support from prospective funders
  • Leads recruitment and staffing for each new program, including hiring and mentoring the director who will lead it, then guides that director through a transition and hands off leadership
  • Helps build and manage each program’s budget and staffing in collaboration with the operations team, and refines Sightline’s method for program development with each cycle

An incomplete list of new program ideas that Sightline has considered, and that the Principal Director could add to, scout and vet includes:

  1. Transportation. Reviving and expanding Sightline’s past work: congestion pricing, building transit and infrastructure far more affordably, autonomous vehicles of all kinds, traffic safety, e-bikes.
  2. Climate migration, population, and demographic change. Sightline has started preliminary research in this area
  3. Rural Cascadia. A reboot of Sightline’s former Farms and Forests program: alternative meats, a critical rethinking of the usual green narrative on agriculture (e.g., We Are Eating the Earth), virtual fencing in place of barbed wire, beaver reintroduction for watershed restoration.
  4. Biological diversity. An area we have neglected in recent years: orcas and salmon, amphibians, birds, bats, and the “insect apocalypse.” Maybe even proposing to rewild half of Cascadia, after E.O. Wilson’s Half Earth.
  5. Artificial intelligence. What it means for our future. How our region should respond. What states can do while the federal government equivocates. And the environmental costs and benefits of data centers.

These are starting points, not a shortlist. Vetting them, and surfacing areas we haven’t considered, is work the Principal Director would do in collaboration with our research staff and senior colleagues.

Desired Skills and Experience

  • Substantial experience at a senior level in policy research, advocacy, journalism, or a related field, including work you initiated rather than inherited
  • Track record of conducting and publishing original, in-depth policy research that changed minds, with demonstrated ability to become credible quickly in fields that are new to you
  • Skilled writer and public speaker, comfortable serving as a senior spokesperson with media, policymakers, and other stakeholders
  • Strong strategic thinker who divines smart ways to influence policy through research, communications, and advocacy
  • Experience contributing to fundraising, including identifying and cultivating relationships with prospective funders and writing proposals and reports
  • Experience engaging policymakers to translate research into policy influence; competence in building unusual coalitions is a plus
  • Experience leading a new initiative, program, or team from early concept through launch— setting strategy, defining goals, and building a team
  • Commitment to Sightline’s mission and values.

Deep subject-matter expertise in one of Sightline’s current or potential program areas is a bonus, not a requirement. Sightline believes in mentoring talent and providing opportunities for growth. We’ve intentionally built flexibility into this role, and we’re open to candidates who may not yet meet every qualification listed, if they bring strong foundational skills, sharp instincts, and a clear ability to grow into the responsibilities described. If you see yourself in this work, we encourage you to apply.

Your First Year:

The early months will be about getting to know Sightline: how we work, how we choose what to work on, and how our research, communications, and advocacy fit together. At the same time, you’ll work with the Executive Director to identify and vet possible program areas against our criteria, then bring a recommendation forward. Once an area is chosen, your focus will shift to original research and publishing, building the program’s strategy, and beginning to cultivate funders and coalition partners. Throughout, you’ll work closely with our communications, development, and research teams.

Compensation and Benefits

The salary range for the Principal Director level is $166,000-185,000, plus a 401K employer contribution of 10 percent of salary with no match required. That contribution is added to pay, not subtracted from it: someone earning $170,000 receives an additional $17,000 in their retirement account, for total compensation of $187,000.

As part of our commitment to equity and to reduce bias, Sightline has salary bands for each position level. Employees can earn annual merit raises and periodic promotions, and we support team members along their career pathways with mentoring, training, and learning opportunities.

Benefits also include:

  • 95% premium coverage for medical, dental, and vision insurance for the employee and partial coverage for dependents
  • 4 weeks of paid vacation
  • 12 paid holidays annually
  • 2 weeks of paid health, wellness, and care leave, plus access to a shared pool of additional leave for special circumstances
  • 12 weeks paid parental leave
  • A 3-month paid sabbatical every 7 years
  • A $200 monthly remote work stipend
  • Regular staff gatherings for in-person connection

As a nonprofit, Sightline is a qualifying employer for the federal Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) program. Our staff work hard and enjoy balanced lives and a collegial organizational culture.

Location:

Sightline is a virtual-first organization. Our staff, contractors, and fellows live and work in all parts of Cascadia. This position is therefore remote, and you may work at home or in a co-working facility of your choice, but you must live and work in Cascadia: Alaska, British Columbia, Idaho, Montana, Oregon, or Washington. The role requires travel to represent Sightline with policymakers, funders, and allies as well as participation in Sightline retreats and meetings.

To Apply

Please include, in this order:

  • A cover letter expressing your qualification for this position along with why you want it. Sightline is a mission-driven organization; we take seriously your motivation and ability to communicate it persuasively.
  • Your resume
  • A brief, published writing sample that showcases your ability to write clearly, succinctly, and compellingly in a style similar to Sightline’s. You may attach the sample or include a link. Our preference is for writing samples that include analysis or recommendations related to a public policy issue. Sightline takes excellent quality research and writing extremely seriously—we’re a think tank!—so your writing sample is key in your evaluation.

None of your application packet should be written by artificial intelligence; Sightline uses A.I. in several ways but not for composing text.

Please assemble all application materials in a single PDF with the naming convention LastName_FirstName_Position. We review applications that include all three; please reach out if the format is a barrier. Please click Apply, fi ll out the form and submit your single PDF.

The application deadline is November 15, and applications received by that date will be given priority. We will accept and review applications until the position is filled. Interviews will take place from mid-November to mid-December, and we will likely invite finalists to complete a work assignment that is designed to test their skills in the specific functions required for the position. We anticipate extending an offer in late December or early January.

Sightline Institute is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified candidates are encouraged to apply. Applicants will not be discriminated against because of race, color, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, religion, national origin, citizenship status, disability, ancestry, marital status, veteran status, medical condition or any protected category prohibited by local, state or federal laws.

jobs.excerpt: About Redesign Group The Redesign Group is a global technology and cybersecurity Solution Provider leveraging design thinking, interdependent subject matter expertise, and emerging technology solutions to help organizations achieve meaningful transformation.
jobs.description:
About Redesign Group

The Redesign Group is a global technology and cybersecurity Solution Provider leveraging design thinking, interdependent subject matter expertise, and emerging technology solutions to help organizations achieve meaningful transformation. Our globally diverse team members, partnerships with strategic technology manufacturers, and cybersecurity services position us to be a business partner that’s ready for what’s next.

We live by our core values of operating in the service of others, being problem solvers, and focusing on long term partnerships. You’ll excel at Redesign if you thrive in a rewarding environment that moves quickly, challenges you to grow and fosters collaboration. We seek candidates with a hands-on customer-first approach, robust interpersonal and communication skills, strong work ethic and excellent time management. While teamwork is expected, the ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment is crucial.

Job Description

The Controller will lead the day-to-day accounting and tax operations – the monthly close, reporting across four legal entities in four countries, revenue and cost accounting, tax and internal controls underneath it all. This role is central to building the financial infrastructure, reporting discipline, and controls needed to support a growing multi-revenue-stream technology and services business.

Reporting to the VP of Finance, you will lead a team spanning general accounting, tax, accounts payable, accounts receivable, and billing — including two direct managers, the Accounting Manager and the Tax Manager. We seek candidates who are hands on leaders, would rather build process than inherit one, are excited about what AI can do to improve workflows and thrive in a fast-moving environment.

Key Responsibilities

Close, Consolidation & Reporting

  • Set the close standard and calendar, driving towards a consistent close within 10 business days that gives leadership real insight into business operations
  • Review and approve the financial statements, reporting package, account reconciliations, and supporting schedules
  • Own multi-entity reporting across the US, UK, Canada, and France as a controlled group, including transfer pricing arrangements and foreign currency translation
  • Govern the chart of accounts, holding consistent treatment across entities, revenue streams, and cost streams
  • Partner with a new FP&A team on the execution of the financial plan —this role owns the actuals and department-level reporting to leaders, with FP&A owning the plan

Revenue & Cost Accounting

  • Oversee accounting across the company’s revenue streams: product resale, software subscriptions, maintenance and renewals, cybersecurity, and professional and managed services
  • Develop and own the cost allocation methodology used to report gross margin by product and service line, reporting meaningful insights into the profitability of each business unit
  • Collaborate with Sales Operations to approve accounting positions on new, non-standard, and judgment-heavy transactions

Tax

  • Own the tax function in partnership with the Tax Manager, covering federal, state and local income tax, sales and use tax, VAT, and Canadian indirect tax
  • Manage multi-state and multi-country registrations and nexus as the company grows

Systems, Controls & Audit

  • Serve as the accounting system owner for QuickBooks, including the integrity of the general ledger
  • Partner with Business Systems Developers and Sales Operations to strengthen the Salesforce-to-QuickBooks workflow supporting bookings, billing, and revenue recognition
  • Design and maintain internal controls, and prepare the company for its first external audit
  • Own sales commission and incentive compensation calculations, accrual methodology, and reporting
  • Oversee payroll in partnership with People Operations — payroll accounting and reconciliation across four entities, plus the controls over pay changes, approvals, and off-cycle runs
  • Own the expense policy and spend management program, ensuring policy is current, communicated, and enforced
  • Support diligence and reporting requests as the business scales
  • Identify and implement process improvements and controls across month end close, financial reporting, AP and spend management, customer billing, AR, and sales commission reporting.

Team Leadership

  • Lead, develop and mentor a growing accounting team, including setting individual development goals and supporting career growth as the team scales
  • Build organizational structure and role clarity within the accounting function as headcount grows, including identifying when and where to add capacity
  • Set priorities and workload across the team to meet close deadlines and reporting commitments
  • Establish team norms, documentation standards, and cross-training practices to reduce key-person risk as the company expands
  • Act as a key partner to the VP of Finance on team capacity planning, structure and hiring needs
  • Model and reinforce a culture of accuracy, accountability, and continuous improvement

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field; CPA preferred
  • 8+ years of progressive accounting experience, including people management, with at least 2 years in a Controller or Assistant Controller capacity
  • Demonstrated experience building or scaling an accounting team, including hiring, structuring roles, and developing staff
  • Strong GAAP knowledge, particularly revenue recognition and COGS matching across multiple revenue streams
  • Experience in a technology, MSP/VAR, or subscription and services-based business strongly preferred
  • International, multi-entity experience strongly preferred
  • Experience partnering cross-functionally with leaders, particularly on topics with financial and compliance implications
  • Hands-on experience with QuickBooks (or comparable ERP) and CRM-to-GL revenue workflows; Experience with accounting system migration a plus; Salesforce experience a plus
  • Track record of owning and improving the monthly close process
  • Experience supporting an audit, financial statement restatement, or transaction diligence process is a plus
  • Strong communicator, comfortable with non-finance stakeholders, auditors, and outside advisors

Additional Compensation: This position is eligible for discretionary incentive compensation and/or bonus opportunities based on individual and company performance.

Benefits

We offer a comprehensive benefits package which may include:

  • Medical , Dental, and Vision Insurance
  • 401(k) retirement plan with company match (annual dollar cap applied)
  • Flexible time off plan
  • 15 paid holidays
  • Sick leave (amount varies by state requirements and is at least the minimum required by any state)
  • Short-term and long-term disability
  • Life insurance
  • Paid parental leave

We’re an Equal Opportunity and Affirmative Action Employer and welcome applicants from all backgrounds. We consider qualified candidates without regard to any legally protected status. This role is subject to applicable employment laws based on work location. In compliance with pay transparency laws, the compensation range for this role is included, with final pay based on experience, skills, and location. We participate in E-Verify to confirm employment eligibility and are happy to provide reasonable accommodations throughout the hiring process—just let us know how we can help.
