jobs.title: Principal Software Engineer, Power Applications
jobs.excerpt: Karman is a fast-growing NVIDIA-backed AI company enabling AI data centers to dynamically orchestrate power and unlock more compute capacity from existing energy infrastructure.
jobs.description:
Karman is a fast-growing NVIDIA-backed AI company enabling AI data centers to dynamically orchestrate power and unlock more compute capacity from existing energy infrastructure. For over a decade, we have applied AI to the electric grid — bringing real-time visibility and power-flow control to complex energy infrastructure. Our Karman platform, built on a custom NVIDIA module, brings that same capability to AI data centers, giving operators a way to better use the power already available to them.

The Power Applications team takes power control and orchestration algorithms from idea to production. We own the complete end-to-end process: developing power control and orchestration algorithms, translating them into deployable applications, and owning the deployment and maintenance of those applications in the field. As the Technical Lead, Power Applications, you will coordinate data scientists and software engineers to produce these applications, define repeatable and scalable workflows that let the team deliver efficiently, and act as the technical interface to other teams on the stack.

This is a leadership role. While you will still spend meaningful time in the codebase, a large part of the work is communication, coordination, and project management. Your leverage comes from the designs you set, the standards you hold, the engineers you develop, and your ability to keep cross-functional work moving.
Success in this role is measured by driving continuous delivery, building for scale and resilience, and navigating the demands of a rapidly growing company. This position works cross-functionally with product, engineering, and data science teams and is open to fully remote candidates, with periodic travel expected for company retreats and key on-site engagements.

Responsibilities
  • Enable the Power Applications team to own the end-to-end lifecycle of Utilidata's power control and orchestration applications, from algorithm development, through translation into deployable software, to deployment and ongoing maintenance in production
  • Directly contribute to the Power Applications codebase and work with the team to define and own code quality standards and engineering workflows
  • Serve as the senior individual contributor coordinating data scientists and software engineers, aligning the group on design and quality through architecture and code review
  • Design continuous delivery workflows that bridge algorithm development and production, including the path from prototype code (e.g., Python) to the deployed application's language (e.g., Rust), so work moves to production smoothly and repeatably
  • Act as the technical interface between Power Applications and other teams on the stack, establishing clear system boundaries, data contracts, and power application SLAs
  • Contribute to system architecture discussions for the Karman platform as a whole, ensuring the subsystems that support power-flow control fit coherently into that wider architecture
  • Build for reliability and scale so power applications run continuously across experimentation, staging, and deployed environments.
Minimum Qualifications
  • 10+ years of software engineering experience, including a track record of technical leadership on complex production systems
  • Demonstrated ability to lead engineers through architecture, code review, and mentorship, and to raise the technical bar of a team
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with substantial experience working directly with stakeholders across teams
  • Strong project management and technical planning skills — sequencing work, managing cross-team dependencies, translating product requirements into technical designs
  • Strong foundation in distributed systems and reliability engineering: fault tolerance, graceful degradation, observability, and testing for systems that cannot go down
  • Experience taking software from prototype to hardened production, ideally where the platform and requirements were still evolving
  • Proficiency in Python and at least one systems language (C++, Rust, or Go)
  • Willingness to travel up to 10% of time
Enhanced Qualifications (Nice to Have)
  • Hands-on experience with real-time, low-latency, or control systems : software that must respond within strict time bounds and behave predictably under load
  • Experience with edge or embedded computing, especially on NVIDIA platforms (Jetson-class devices, CUDA, or NVML)
  • Background in power systems, energy, industrial control, robotics, or another physical-world real-time domain)
  • Experience productionizing ML models or algorithms in collaboration with data science teams
Salary Range: $180,000 to $220,000 base compensation depending on experience and level, plus stock options. This role spans multiple job levels; final level and compensation will be determined based on the candidate's experience.

Location: This position can be performed remotely from anywhere in the United States.

Our Commitments:
Karman values the diversity of our team. We are committed to:

jobs.title: Commercial Contract Specialist
jobs.excerpt: Managing pricing and rebates shouldn’t be a hassle.
jobs.description:
Managing pricing and rebates shouldn’t be a hassle. Enable’s intelligent platform is built for the speed of today’s market, eliminating disconnects between pricing strategy and rebate execution. We help companies to increase profitability and simplify the complex with accurate, AI-powered insights, real-time performance monitoring, agreement optimization, and simplified rebate management.
After securing $291M in Series A-D funding and acquiring Flintfox in 2025, Enable is positioned for continued, significant growth. Since the launch of our flagship product in 2016, we have been rapidly scaling our client base, product offerings, and built a team of top-tier professionals committed to reshaping the industry.
Want a glimpse into life at Enable? Visit our Life at Enable page to learn how you can be part of our journey.

Job Summary

As the Commercial Contracts Specialist, you will serve as the primary commercial resource for Enable's sales team and the company's front line for legal intake and triage. You will draft, review, redline, and negotiate customer and vendor agreements to keep deals moving while managing commercial and contractual risk, and you will own the intake and triage of legal matters across the business — determining what can be handled internally versus what requires outside support, and managing the panel of outside counsel and advisors engaged to support the company.

This role combines hands-on commercial contract work with legal operations responsibility, and is well suited to someone who is a strong, practical negotiator and can move quickly between contract detail and broader legal-operations judgment calls.

Duties and Responsibilities - Commercial Contracts

    • Draft, review, redline, and negotiate customer agreements and, as needed, vendor agreements in collaboration with relevant business leader) negotiation of vendors as needed. This could include subscriptions, properties, utilities, advisors, agencies, etc.

    • Own the company Non-Disclosure-Agreement letters and wording.

    • Serve as the primary commercial resource for the sales team — for review of contractual terms and conditions and providing feedback on how they compare to terms reviewed for similar situations and what recommendations might improve Enable’s overall position in a contractual negotiation.

    • Manage contract risk across the customer and vendor contract portfolio.

    • Ensure that existing vendor agreements are monitored and proactively managed ensuring they are renewed in an orderly and considered fashion with a focus on maximising value for Enable.

    • Identify areas for improvement and continually drive performance and business results across vendor portfolio.

Duties and Responsibilities - Legal Operations

    • Own intake and triage of legal matters for the company, determining what can be handled internally and what requires outside support.

    • Select and engage outside firms and individual attorneys for matters requiring outside support.

    • Manage the panel of external counsel, IP counsel, and insurance brokers.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities (KSAs)

    • Experience drafting, reviewing, redlining, and negotiating commercial agreements (customer and/or vendor); formal legal training is not required.

    • Strong understanding of commercial terms and conditions, commercial contracts.

    • Strong negotiation and communication skills, with the ability to act as a trusted commercial partner to a sales organization.

    • Able to influence others and build effective relationships with the business and external stakeholders.

    • Sound judgment for triaging legal and contractual risk, including knowing when a matter needs outside counsel.

    • Comfortable managing relationships with outside law firms, individual attorneys, and other external advisors.

    • Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage a high volume of contracts and matters concurrently.

    • Ability to explain contractual and legal concepts clearly to non-legal stakeholders.

    • Reliable, accurate, and able to work independently with a continuous-improvement mindset.

Required Education and Experience

    • 5+ years' experience drafting, reviewing, redlining, and negotiating commercial agreements.

    • Bachelor's degree, or equivalent practical experience gained through a contracts, procurement, or legal-support career path; formal legal qualification is not required.

    • Demonstrated ownership of customer-side agreements end to end, including NDAs, order forms, master services or subscription agreements, and associated schedules.

    • Experience negotiating vendor, supplier, or procurement agreements and managing renewals across a contract portfolio.

    • Experience acting as the primary commercial contact for a sales organisation in a fast-moving, target-driven environment.

    • Experience instructing and working with outside counsel or external advisors on matters falling outside internal capability.

jobs.excerpt: Sales Development Representative Location: Cape Town, Western Cape, South Africa (Fully Remote)Engagement Type: Contractor Working Hours: Monday to Friday - ﻿12:30am to 9:00am SAST Salary: R18 000 - R24 000 ( Based on Experience ) ﻿ ﻿﻿ Why this role existsOur client is an AI platform used by more than 1,000 real estate agencies across Australia and New Zealand.

Sales Development Representative

Location: Cape Town, Western Cape, South Africa

(Fully Remote)

Engagement Type: Contractor

Working Hours: Monday to Friday - ﻿12:30am to 9:00am SAST

Salary: R18 000 - R24 000 ( Based on Experience )
﻿

﻿﻿

Why this role exists

Our client is an AI platform used by more than 1,000 real estate agencies across Australia and New Zealand. Their free Agent Grader scores an agent's digital visibility and ranks them against their market, and it has become their best acquisition asset: agents claim a score, see where they sit, and get recommendations they can only act on with a paid plan. In a few short weeks over 300 agents have already claimed their profiles. The problem is what happens next. This role owns that gap. You turn scores into conversations, and conversations into booked meetings for the people who close. You will be the first dedicated sales hire in the business.

What you will own

1. Working every Grader lead, and building the list when inbound does not fill the day. Every agent and agency that claims a score, attends a webinar or comes off an event list gets worked to a decision within an agreed window. Nothing sits untouched. Where that does not fill your day, you build the working list yourself out of the Grader database and the targeting model below, inside the audiences and priority order marketing has set. You are never waiting for someone to hand you names.

﻿﻿2. Multi-channel outbound. Sequenced email through Instantly, LinkedIn, and phone into a defined afternoon calling block. Value-offer first (their score, their ranking, their recommendations), never a cold pitch for a demo.

﻿﻿3. Prioritisation, qualification and routing. You will not work the list from the top down. We are building an Agency Opportunity Score built from four signal layers that identifies the signals that show they are more likely to convert: Grader and DVI position. Score, tier and visibility gap across the 38,000 plus agents we already hold data on, plus whether they have claimed their profile and how recently. Rent roll strength. Proxied from rental listing counts and property management headcount. A strong rent roll means cash flow and budget in a soft market, and these agencies are the consolidators absorbing exiting agents and rent rolls. Market activity. Listing volumes, days on market, and share of stock under $1M by suburb and region.

﻿4. Booked, held meetings. The metric is meetings that happen and are accepted by the person taking them, not meetings booked.

﻿﻿5. CRM discipline. Every touch, outcome and next step logged in HubSpot the same day. If it is not in HubSpot it did not happen. You will also flag data problems you find rather than working around them.

6. Feedback to marketing and product. Weekly, in writing: which openers worked, which objections repeat, which Grader scores convert, what agents asked for that we do not have.

﻿

﻿Requirements

﻿- Two years or more of outbound SDR or BDR work into small business or SME buyers, with evidence of consistent, self-directed activity, not inbound order taking.
- Written English that a suspicious, time-poor agent will read to the end.

  • Comfort on the phone with people who did not ask you to call, and the resilience to keep dialling in a soft market.
  • Startup temperament. There is no enablement library, no manager three metres away, and no established process. You will be expected to work out the answer, propose it, and then document it for whoever comes next.
  • Fluency with a CRM (HubSpot preferred), sequencing tools (Instantly preferred), Claude and comfort building and segmenting your own working lists from a database rather than waiting for one.
  • Willingness to work a shifted day that gives at least four hours of live overlap with the Australian eastern business day. From October that means an early start.

﻿

Preferred

  • Experience selling into real estate, property services or another relationship-driven, licence-based industry.
  • Experience in a product-led business where a free tool feeds a sales conversation.
  • Familiarity with Instantly, HubSpot sequences, LinkedIn Sales Navigator, or similar.

﻿

jobs.description:
Are you looking for more than a job? At World Vision Canada we offer challenging careers that change the lives of children all over the world and it will change yours too. Come and be part of a team of 400 Canadians with a vision for the world: Life in all its fullness for every child.

You will experience Christian faith in action helping to make real and lasting change in the lives of the world’s most vulnerable children. Join the World Vision Canada team and be part of a powerful and effective force for good:

For Children. For Change. For Life.

Position: Data Architect Reports to: Director, Data Intelligence Position Term: Full Time Permanent Primary Location: Mississauga, Ontario, Canada Workplace Type: Remote (Within Canada)

Job Purpose

The Data Architect is responsible for the design, governance and integrity of World Vision Canada's data architecture. The role defines how data is structured, stored, integrated and made available for reporting, analytics and artificial intelligence, and translates business information requirements into a well-governed and reusable data foundation. It ensures that data is managed as an enterprise asset that is consistent across systems, reliable for decision-making, and able to support the organization as its technology environment changes, thereby supporting the organization's mission.

Reporting to the Director, Data Intelligence, the incumbent develops the organization's data architecture framework and principles for the Director's approval and is thereafter accountable for their application across the enterprise. The incumbent owns the data architecture for the multi-year transformation program and sets the multi-year direction and roadmap for the organization's data architecture and platform. Support for day-to-day operations is provided on an as-available basis and is ad-hoc in nature. This is a hands-on role, with results achieved through modernizing data flows, publishing standards, documentation and design reviews.

Responsibilities

  • Designs the enterprise data architecture. Develops the conceptual, logical and physical data architecture, including the data platform, canonical data models, and the standards that govern how data is structured, stored and moved. Establishes the framework and principles that govern this work and holds all designs, internal and vendor, to them.
  • Develops and presents the data architecture for senior leadership approval. Prepares and presents the data architecture, its roadmap and material design decisions to senior leadership for approval, frames the options and the trade-offs between them, and sets the multi-year direction for the organization's data architecture and platform.
  • Defines data integration and interoperability standards. Establishes the contract-first patterns, interfaces and reusable standards by which systems exchange data, including schema and interface contracts defined in advance of build. This includes the standards for secure data-sharing with federated partner organizations across the wider World Vision partnership, distinct from the organization's own enterprise data governance which the role helps uphold. Sets the data architecture requirements that solution designs must satisfy, rules on data design questions arising within solution architecture, and confirms that individual solutions stay coherent with the wider data architecture.
  • Architects governed, reusable data products. Designs trustworthy, well-defined data products and master data structures, including consolidated master records and analytical models, that support reporting, analytics and machine learning. Ensures these are documented, discoverable and reusable across business areas rather than rebuilt for each initiative.
  • Establishes data quality, master data and lifecycle standards. Defines the controls for data quality, master data management, retention and remediation, and requires delivery teams to apply them in day-to-day practice. Sets quality and design standards at a level sufficient for data to be consumed reliably by analytics and artificial intelligence, including requirements for completeness, consistency, labelling and documented meaning. Monitors adherence, directs the remediation of data quality and data definition issues at source, and withholds acceptance where the controls are not met.
  • Sets standards for AI and machine learning data use and platform portability. Defines how analytical and machine learning workloads consume governed data, and designs for platform portability so that the organization avoids undue dependence on any single vendor or platform.
  • Establishes data security and protection standards. Defines how data is classified, protected and accessed, with particular attention to sensitive information and to data relating to donors, employees, and vulnerable populations, including children participating in the organization's programs. Ensures protection, privacy and access controls are included in designs from the outset, and that designs meet or exceed regulatory and organizational obligations.
  • Produces and maintains architecture documentation. Produces and maintains data architecture documentation, including conceptual, logical and physical data models, current and target state reference architectures, data flow and integration diagrams, architecture decision records and standards documentation. Maintains these as the reference used by delivery teams and as the record of architecture governance.
  • Governs solution and vendor designs through to delivery. Reviews solution and vendor designs against data architecture standards, prepares and reviews architecture decision records, and confirms alignment before designs proceed. Guides delivery teams through implementation, holds delivered systems to the architecture, and adjusts the architecture where implementation shows it to be wrong.

Qualifications

Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
  • Enterprise-architecture or cloud data-platform certification, for example TOGAF or a recognized cloud data credential. Preferred.

Experience

  • Ten or more years working in data management disciplines such as data modelling, data engineering or data science.
  • Five or more years in data architecture, including the design of lakehouse or warehouse-native patterns and of batch and streaming data flows in Snowflake and other cloud data platforms.
  • Demonstrated accountability for an enterprise data architecture, including setting standards adopted across delivery teams and vendors, and presenting architecture direction to senior leadership for approval.
  • Demonstrated delivery of master-data and golden-record solutions, and of governed, reusable data products, as well as warehouse-native customer data platforms.
  • Demonstrated experience setting data design direction for solution architects and delivery partners within an established technology or architecture function.
  • Experience designing data protection, classification and access controls for sensitive data.
  • Experience in a nonprofit or mission-driven organization. Preferred.

Technical skills

  • Defining data and application-programming-interface contracts in advance of build, including the use of schema registries and contract testing.
  • Advanced data modelling across conceptual, logical and physical layers, relational and dimensional, and strong SQL.
  • Familiarity with modern transformation frameworks, for example dbt, ELT patterns, and orchestration tooling, sufficient to define standards and review implementations.
  • Familiarity with Python or similar scripting languages for prototyping and automation.
  • Understanding of continuous integration and delivery and automated testing practices for data, including contract and schema testing, sufficient to embed them in standards and review vendor delivery against them.
  • Command of modern data architecture paradigms, including data mesh, data fabric and lakehouse, sufficient to select between them and defend the choice.
  • Familiarity with data catalog and metadata management tooling.
  • Proficiency with architecture modelling notations and tooling for producing models and diagrams, for example ArchiMate or UML.
  • Experience working in environments using Enterprise Agile frameworks.

Soft skills and competencies

  • Communicates clearly with both technical specialists and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Builds agreement on design direction across technical and business teams.
  • Applies sound judgement to complex and ambiguous design problems, balancing long-term architectural integrity against near-term delivery needs.
  • Records design decisions, applies standards consistently, and supports recommendations with evidence.

Why Consider Us?

  • Our competitive compensation & benefits include:
  • Health Spending Account
  • Up to 6% matched pension contributions
  • Parental leave top-up
  • Generous paid vacation, sick days, wellness and personal days
  • Office closed extra days before long weekends (6x/year)
  • World Vision Canada has consistently been awarded Canada and GTA top employer awards.
  • We are Canada’s largest development, relief, and advocacy non-profit organization.
  • We embody an Agile mindset here.

This is a current vacancy that we are actively recruiting for. The salary range represents the expected compensation for this role and is provided in accordance with Ontario’s pay transparency requirements under the Employment Standards Act.

Placement within the range will be determined based on relevant skills, experience, qualifications, and internal equity. The final offer will reflect the successful candidate’s background and demonstrated capabilities.

We shall never rest while children suffer in situations that can be changed.

jobs.excerpt: We're an AI-enabled corporate & personal tax prep firm, supporting 1,000+ of the most innovative founders and their companies — including Cursor, Cognition Labs, and ModRetro.
jobs.description:
We're an AI-enabled corporate & personal tax prep firm, supporting 1,000+ of the most innovative founders and their companies — including Cursor, Cognition Labs, and ModRetro. We work with hundreds of executives, HNWIs, and venture capitalists as part of our corporate offering, combining corporate tax, personal taxes, R&D credits, and bookkeeping in one firm to make tax season take as little of our clients' time as possible, without leaving any tax savings on the table.

We're growing quickly, well-funded, and backed by XYZ Ventures, Susa Ventures, and Haystack Ventures, alongside operators from Ramp, Stripe, Deel, and others. And while we may have just gotten started a little over two years ago, this isn't our first rodeo:

  • Nick Abouzeid (cofounder & CEO) ran three growth teams at Ramp and previously led marketing at MainStreet ($3M → $15M ARR in 2 years)

  • Kyle Christenson (cofounder & Head of Tax) spent six years auditing at the IRS, then joined MainStreet to handle their most complex claims

Why this role is different

Most tax work in this industry gets jammed into the back half of busy season by people who are tired and over-leveraged. We've built the firm so the technical experts on the most complex corporate returns get the time, source documents, and tooling to do the work right.

You're the technical backbone for our corporate portfolio (either 1120 or 1065/1120-S, depending your background). Our Client Success Managers own the non-tax administrative work; you make sure the work that leaves the firm is bulletproof.

We optimize for the things that actually matter to the work:

  • Own technical quality – you decide what "great" looks like in our 1065 and 1120-S work, and you keep us honest about it as we scale.

  • No time-tracking – we don't track hours. We value results and empathy over arbitrary time-tracking.

  • Build, don't repeat – we're a tech-forward firm. When you spot a recurring issue, you don't just fix it on this return; you partner with engineering to make sure it's caught automatically on the next one.

  • Judgment over throughput – we'd rather you hold a return for one more day to get a §754 election right than push it out the door on schedule.

We’re looking for a technically strong, hands-on U.S. Tax Manager to own the quality of our partnership and S-corporation tax work. You’ll be the person our team, founders, and CFOs rely on when the answer is not obvious—and when getting it right matters.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys digging into source documents, solving complex tax questions, and turning technical conclusions into accurate returns, defensible workpapers, and practical advice.

What you'll do

  • Be the go-to technical expert. Own the quality and accuracy of complex Forms 1065 and 1120-S, including Schedules K-1 and K-2/K-3. Research complex or unfamiliar tax issues, identify reasonable assumptions, document supportable conclusions, and explain the recommended approach clearly to founders, CFOs, and internal teams.

  • Handle the technically complex work. Lead the team’s day-to-day workstream preparation and review of complex partnership and S corporation tax returns, including Schedule K-1/K-3 processing, inside and outside tax basis calculations, debt allocations, and S-corporation shareholder basis and accumulated adjustments account calculations.

  • Support the full entity life cycle. Advise on and review the tax treatment of formations, contributions, interest transfers, redemptions, distributions, mergers, restructurings, and liquidations.

  • Read the source materials. Analyze operating and partnership agreements, cap tables, distribution waterfalls, transaction documents, and board consents. Translate their legal and economic terms into clean, supportable workpapers, allocations, and tax returns.

  • Navigate multistate issues and address international reporting. Provide technical guidance on state income and franchise taxes, nexus, apportionment, composite and withholding filings, and state pass-through entity tax elections; Review matters involving foreign partners, Schedules K-2 and K-3, and withholding and information-reporting requirements, including Forms 8804/8805 and 1042/1042-S.

  • Partner with Client Success Managers. They will manage much of the administrative coordination; you will provide the technical backbone that makes our work accurate, defensible, and valuable to clients. Manage competing priorities, anticipate risks, flag issues early, and lead the team in meeting filing and client-delivery deadlines.

  • Use technology thoughtfully. Lean on our technology stack to improve efficiency and consistency while knowing when professional judgment and hands-on review are non-negotiable. Able to identify errors and unsupported positions, provide actionable technical feedback, and turn recurring issues into repeatable processes and training.

What makes you a fit

  • CPA or EA designation

  • Five or more years of hands-on U.S. tax experience focused on flow-through entities. At least two years of tax planning and compliance experience with operating partnerships and/or S corporations

  • Demonstrated ability to independently prepare or review basis, capital account, special allocation, Section 704(c), and Section 743(b) calculations

  • Ability to read partnership and operating agreements and connect their economic provisions to the related tax allocations and reporting

  • Strong tax research skills and the ability to produce clear, defensible technical conclusions and workpapers

  • Ability to review and develop team members while maintaining accountability for quality and deadlines

  • Clear communication skills, sound judgment, and a habit of identifying and escalating issues early

  • A mindset that goes beyond getting a return out the door—you want the work to be accurate, well-supported, and defensible

Nice to haves

  • Experience with 704(b) book adjustments, private fund partnerships, GP/LP structures, carries-interest or management-fee-waiver allocations, and multi-tier flow through structures

  • Experience with targeted capital accounts, complex distribution waterfalls, disguised-sale rules, and partnership-interest transactions

  • Experience with individual and blocker corporations, and equity-compensation reporting

  • Experience with transaction modeling, tax planning, tax notices, or federal and state examinations

  • Experience developing technical guidance or delivering training to tax professionals

  • Prior exposure to a technology-forward or automated tax workflow

  • Interest in helping shape the future of a product-first, technology-enabled tax firm

What we offer

  • Generous cash comp with meaningful equity upside

  • Fully remote, with twice-yearly company offsites

  • A modern tech stack — no SmartVault, no ShareFile, no PDF email tag — built specifically to make complex flow-through work faster and cleaner

  • A global, ex-Big-4 production and review bench so you spend your time on judgment work, not data entry

  • A book of complex flow-through clients spanning VC-backed startups, multi-tier funds, and high-growth SMBs

  • The chance to define how a tech-forward firm handles complex corporate work

About the opportunity

We are hiring a Director, Public Health Systems to take a proven hospital quality programme and make it run on its own. The programme helps private and public hospitals improve the quality of care they offer.

It has grown across India, and government partners are now on board. The next phase is to make the programme independent and self-funded, and to grow it several times over.

The role

This is a role for a builder. The model works and has been tested at scale. It now needs someone to move it from donor funding to self-sustaining.

You will set up and grow multiple independent entities to run the programme, each built to pay for itself. That means designing their structure, governance and revenue, putting the right teams in place, and mentoring their leaders for two to three years until each one runs without outside support. As the model spreads to new states and, over time, other countries, you will build the next ones.

We need someone who gets things done, not someone who only advises. The direction is largely clear, and the work now is in making it happen.

Key responsibilities

  • Set up multiple independent entities to run the programme, and build the revenue models that make each one self-funded.
  • Grow the programme across medical institutions and states, and repeat the model in new geographies over time.
  • Build and manage relationships with medical institutions, government and other key partners.
  • Lead a team of 20 people directly and coordinate 50 people across partners.
  • Put leadership teams in place for each entity and mentor them until they can run on their own, within two to three years.

What you will bring

These are essential for the role:

  • Leadership: you have led large teams and worked through partners you don't manage directly, at a senior level.
  • Networks in the healthcare ecosystem: you have strong, working relationships with doctors and medical associations, hospital accreditation and quality bodies, and government health systems. You can pick up the phone and get a meeting.
  • Experience building something: you have set up a business, a new unit or an independent entity and made it financially sustainable. You understand revenue, pricing, governance and what it takes to hand something over to others.
  • A record of getting things done: you have delivered results on the ground, not only designed the strategy. We will look for this clearly in references.
  • Education: an MBA or equivalent, with solid healthcare experience.
  • Comfort with travel and senior stakeholders: you are at ease travelling often and presenting the work to senior doctors, regulators and government.

We welcome candidates from a range of backgrounds. These include pharma and medical affairs, healthcare consulting, hospital networks, professional and industry associations, government advisory, and also the development sector. What matters most is that you combine the networks, the builder's mindset and a record of getting things done.

Location, compensation and terms

  • Location: remote within India, with frequent travel.
  • Compensation: ₹35–40 LPA, based on experience and seniority.
  • Contract: a one-year contract, renewed as the work grows. However, this work would require a commitment of 5-7 years to build.

For people who want to work on AI that matters, in a sector where correctness, trust, and real-world impact count, Kalepa is just getting started.

Our Values (This is important):

Many organizations have a dusty list of corporate values that no one ever follows. Kalepa is not one of those companies. Our values are designed to unlock the potential of our employees.

  • Hustle and Determination - We hire people who take full ownership of their craft and relentlessly pursue excellence with speed and determination. We choose the hard problems and do not give up. This is the foundation of how we work and how we win.

  • Experiment Relentlessly - Many of the problems we face have never been solved before. We tackle them by testing quickly, measuring rigorously, and iterating until we find the path forward. Speed of learning is our advantage.

jobs.excerpt: Practice Medicine the Way You Always Hoped You Would!
jobs.description:
Practice Medicine the Way You Always Hoped You Would!

Heartstrings Pet Hospice is hiring In-Home Hospice and Euthanasia Veterinarians to serve pet families throughout Charleston, Mount Pleasant & Goose Creek, South Carolina and Surrounding Areas.

If you are a compassionate veterinarian looking for a career outside the traditional clinic environment - one with greater professional autonomy, meaningful relationships with pet families, and the time to practice veterinary medicine with intention - Heartstrings Pet Hospice offers a different way to practice.

No waiting room. No double-booked appointment columns. No corporate production dashboard. Just you, a family who loves their pet, and the time and space to provide compassionate end-of-life veterinary care the way you believe it should be provided.

At Heartstrings, our veterinarians provide in-home pet hospice, palliative care, quality-of-life support, and compassionate euthanasia services, helping families navigate one of the most difficult moments of pet ownership in the comfort and privacy of home.

Privately Held. Family-Owned. Doctor-Led.

Heartstrings Pet Hospice is a Privately held, Family-Owned and Doctor-Led Veterinary Practice. We are not a private-equity-owned veterinary group, and we believe veterinarians should have the professional autonomy to practice medicine while maintaining control over the direction of their careers.

And at Heartstrings, WE DO NOT USE VETERINARIAN NON-COMPETE AGREEMENTS.

Not a shortened non-compete.

Not a smaller geographic radius.

Not a so-called “reasonable” restriction.

None!

Your veterinary career should never be held hostage by a contract clause.

Unlike veterinary organizations that restrict where veterinarians can work after leaving, Heartstrings believes talented veterinary professionals should be free to build their careers on their own terms.

We want veterinarians to stay with Heartstrings because they Choose To Stay - because they value the work, the families they serve, their professional autonomy, and the quality of life this type of veterinary medicine can provide.

Your career belongs to you. We would simply like the opportunity to earn the right to be part of it.

If you are searching for a veterinarian job in Charleston, West Ashley, Goose Creek and Summerville, South Carolina & Surrounding Areas and want to explore a career in in-home pet hospice, palliative care, and euthanasia, we would welcome the opportunity to speak with you.

Compassion. Dignity. Respect.
That is what we promise pet families—and what we believe veterinary professionals deserve from the organization they choose to call home.

Who Thrives Here

The veterinarians who thrive at Heartstrings Pet Hospice are often the doctors who have always been especially good at the moments that matter most—the difficult conversations, supporting families through anticipatory grief, and providing compassionate end-of-life veterinary care with empathy, confidence, and clinical judgment.

If you have ever finished a euthanasia appointment and thought, “That was the most meaningful thing I did all week—I just wish I’d had another twenty minutes,” you already understand why veterinarians choose In-Home Pet Hospice and Euthanasia Care.

This role can be an especially meaningful career path for experienced general practice and emergency veterinarians who want to step away from the relentless pace of a traditional veterinary hospital or ER without stepping away from practicing medicine. Instead of crowded appointment schedules and competing demands, our veterinarians can focus on hospice, palliative care, quality-of-life support, pain and symptom management, and peaceful in-home euthanasia while helping families make informed, compassionate decisions for the pets they love.

We also genuinely welcome veterinarians returning to clinical practice, doctors seeking a flexible veterinary career, and veterinarians building a schedule around children, family, travel, or life outside of work.

You spent years becoming a veterinarian. You should not have to choose between practicing meaningful veterinary medicine and having a meaningful life outside of it.

Requirements

Essential Functions & Responsibilities

As an In-Home Hospice and Euthanasia Veterinarian with Heartstrings Pet Hospice, you will provide compassionate, individualized veterinary care to pets and their families in the comfort and privacy of their homes.

  • Provide in-home pet hospice, palliative care, quality-of-life support, pain and symptom management, and compassionate euthanasia services within your assigned service area.
  • Independently travel to scheduled appointments and practice effectively in a mobile veterinary care environment outside of a traditional veterinary hospital or clinic.
  • Perform appropriate physical examinations, clinical assessments, medication administration, sedation, euthanasia, and other veterinary services within the scope of the position and applicable veterinary regulations.
  • Educate and guide pet families through quality-of-life decisions, end-of-life care options, the euthanasia process, and aftercare considerations with empathy and clear professional communication.
  • Maintain accurate, timely, and professional veterinary medical records and clinical documentation for each patient encounter.
  • Communicate professionally and collaboratively with pet families, the Heartstrings veterinary medical team, scheduling and support teams, and referring veterinary professionals.
  • Safely handle, position, and assist with the movement of companion animals during in-home veterinary appointments.
  • Maintain professionalism, clinical independence, sound medical judgment, and reliability while working independently in the field.
  • Consistently demonstrate Heartstrings' commitment to Compassion. Dignity. Respect. in every interaction with patients, families, colleagues, and veterinary partners.

Required Qualifications

  • Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM), Veterinary Medical Doctor (VMD), BVMS, or equivalent veterinary medical degree from an accredited or otherwise qualifying veterinary program.
  • Hold, or be eligible to obtain, an active veterinary license in the state(s) where services will be provided.
  • Possess a valid U.S. driver's license and be able to safely travel between scheduled in-home veterinary appointments.
  • Comfortable working independently as a mobile veterinarian while remaining connected to and supported by the Heartstrings veterinary and operations teams.
  • Demonstrated ability to communicate with empathy and professionalism, particularly during sensitive pet hospice, quality-of-life, and end-of-life conversations.
  • Availability to participate in rotational weekend scheduling as required by the position.
  • Ability to lift and carry up to 50 pounds unassisted and assist with weights up to 100 pounds, with reasonable accommodation where applicable.
  • Ability to perform the physical and logistical requirements associated with providing veterinary care in a variety of residential environments.
  • Successful completion of applicable background and motor vehicle record checks following hire and before the employee's scheduled start date.

Benefits

Where Veterinarians Stay by Choice, Not by Contract.

At Heartstrings Pet Hospice, we believe veterinarians should have more than a meaningful career. They should have the Compensation, Flexibility, Professional Autonomy, Benefits, and Work-Life Balance to build a life they enjoy outside of veterinary medicine, too.

Competitive Compensation & Professional Autonomy

  • Competitive veterinarian compensation designed to recognize your experience, schedule, and contribution to the families you serve
  • Self-managed scheduling with greater control over your professional calendar and work-life balance
  • Supported by a dedicated Scheduling, Operations, and Veterinary Medical Team, allowing you to focus on practicing medicine and caring for families
  • Work for a privately held, Family-Owned and Doctor-Led Veterinary Practice
  • Absolutely NO Veterinarian Non-Compete Agreement - your career and professional future remain yours

Health, Dental & Vision Benefits

Eligible team members have access to a comprehensive benefits package designed to support both individual and family needs, including:

  • Medical insurance
  • Dental insurance
  • Vision insurance
  • Flexible Spending Account (FSA)
  • Dependent Care FSA

Paid Time Off & Family Support

We believe sustainable veterinary careers require meaningful time away from work.

  • Generous Paid Time Off (PTO) for eligible full-time veterinarians
  • PTO that increases with tenure
  • Generous paid parental leave
  • Additional Continuing Education Time Off for eligible veterinarians

Retirement & Financial Protection

  • 401(k) retirement plan
  • Life insurance
  • Short-Term disability insurance
  • Long-Term disability insurance
  • Accidental Death & Dismemberment (AD&D) insurance

Continuing Education & Professional Development

We want our veterinarians to continue learning, growing, and practicing medicine with confidence.

  • Up to $2,000 in annual Continuing Education (CE) allowance
  • Additional CE Paid Time Off
  • CE allowance and paid CE days based on eligible work schedule
  • Ongoing support from an experienced veterinary medical leadership team

Wellness & Additional Perks

  • Pet insurance
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP) providing additional personal and well-being support

And the Benefit No Contract Can Give You Back

No Non-Compete Agreement. Your Career Stays Yours.

We believe veterinarians should have the freedom to determine where and how they practice medicine throughout their careers. We want you to build a career with Heartstrings because you choose to be here, not because a restrictive contract limits what you can do next.

At Heartstrings Pet Hospice, we believe in-home pet hospice, palliative care, and compassionate euthanasia are among the most meaningful services a veterinarian can provide.

If you are looking for a veterinary career with work-life balance, flexible scheduling, professional autonomy, competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits, and no non-compete agreement, we would welcome the opportunity to speak with you.

Heartstrings Pet Hospice
Compassion • Dignity • Respect • Empathy

jobs.title: Principal Speech Data Linguist
jobs.excerpt: Innodata (Nasdaq: INOD) is a global data engineering company.
jobs.description:
Innodata (Nasdaq: INOD) is a global data engineering company. We believe that data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) are inextricably linked. Our mission is to enable the responsible advancement of artificial intelligence by providing the data, evaluation frameworks, and human expertise required to build AI systems that can be trusted at scale. We provide a range of transferable solutions, platforms, and services for Generative AI / AI builders and adopters. In every relationship, we honor our 36+ year legacy delivering the highest quality data and outstanding outcomes for our customers.

Scope of the Role:

As speech and audio models get better, the human role gets harder, not easier — it moves from producing transcripts to defining what a correct one is, adjudicating the cases models still get wrong, and designing the human-in-the-loop workflows that keep improving them. Innodata runs high-volume segmentation and transcription workflows for the customers and frontier labs building these models, and we are hiring a principal-level linguist to own the linguistic standards and quality behind that work — today, and as the workflows evolve alongside the models over the next two years.

This is the applied-expert counterpart to our Speech & Audio Research Scientist. You set the standards the models are trained and measured against, and you understand the big picture: how different transcription and segmentation methods change what a model learns, and how that ripples into the speech and content-understanding systems our partners are building. You know the research and you know the tools — from IPA and acoustic analysis to forced alignment and the ASR engines our partners benchmark against — but your leverage is linguistic judgment and standard-setting at scale, not building models yourself.

What You’ll Own:

  • You will own the linguistic foundation of Innodata's segmentation and transcription work across languages, domains, and use cases. Concretely, you will:
  • Define transcription and segmentation standards, style guides, and annotation conventions — verbatim and clean/intelligent verbatim, IPA and phonetic transcription, timestamping and boundary segmentation, speaker labeling and diarization labels, disfluencies and non-speech events, code-switching, and orthographic conventions.
  • Establish and run the quality frameworks behind that work: rubrics, error taxonomies, adjudication processes, inter-annotator agreement, and human QA at scale.
  • Own the quality lifecycle for transcription and segmentation deliverables end to end — pre-processing and normalization of incoming data, quality checks at the point of acceptance, post-processing and pre-delivery validation against spec, and report creation and packaging for delivery — partnering with delivery operations on execution at scale.
  • Design the human-in-the-loop workflows themselves — deciding where human review, correction, and adjudication add the most value as ASR quality rises, so our experts spend their time on what the models still can't do rather than on what they already can.
  • Handle the linguistically hard cases models fail on — accented and dialectal speech, low-resource and multilingual audio, overlapping speech, domain jargon (medical, legal, technical), and noisy acoustic conditions.
  • Partner with the Speech & Audio Research Scientist to turn model objectives into transcription and segmentation specifications, and to work out how different transcription methods — verbatim versus clean, phonetic versus orthographic, and how audio is segmented and labeled — affect the training and evaluation of ASR, TTS, and speech and content-understanding models.
  • Train, calibrate, and mentor expert transcribers and reviewers, and build the onboarding and calibration that keep quality consistent as the work scales.
  • Represent Innodata's transcription and segmentation approach to the customers and frontier labs we partner with, and contribute to the methodology and best-practice documentation that make our work legible to their teams.

You’ll Thrive in This Role If You Have:

  • Substantial industry experience (typically 8+ years) in transcription, segmentation, and speech-data quality — enough that you have authored standards, not only followed them. This is a principal-level role, and we weight practical depth heavily.
  • A Bachelor's degree in linguistics, phonetics, or computational linguistics, or a closely related field, is required — with a strong foundation in phonetics, phonology, and sociolinguistics so that IPA, prosody, disfluency, dialect, and register are native concepts. An advanced degree is preferred.
  • A big-picture grasp of how transcription and segmentation choices flow downstream into modeling — how different methods change what speech and content-understanding models learn, and therefore which method fits which modeling objective. You can explain to a model builder why a transcription decision matters.
  • Fluency in phonetic transcription and IPA, plus hands-on experience with acoustic and phonetic analysis of speech — spectrograms, formants, pitch and prosody, and segment boundaries — applied to real, messy speech data at scale (for example in Praat).
  • Deep experience with audio segmentation and its conventions — utterance and turn boundaries, timestamping, and speaker and diarization labeling — across real-world audio.
  • Hands-on fluency with the modern speech stack: Whisper and the commercial ASR engines your partners benchmark against (such as AssemblyAI, Deepgram, Rev, and Speechmatics), forced alignment (for example the Montreal Forced Aligner), and annotation tools such as ELAN.
  • Comfort scripting for speech-data work — Python for batch processing, QA, and metrics such as inter-annotator agreement and WER, plus regular expressions and Praat scripting — enough to work fluently with data and pipelines without needing an engineer for every task.
  • Practical data-management skills across the delivery lifecycle — pre-processing, acceptance-stage quality checks, post-processing, pre-delivery validation, and report creation and packaging — so deliverables leave the door correct, consistent, and well documented.
  • Multilingual capability and hands-on experience with accented, dialectal, and code-switched speech; low-resource languages a strong plus.
  • A point of view on how human-in-the-loop workflows should evolve as models improve — where humans stay in the loop, where they move up to adjudication and standard-setting, and how to measure the difference.
  • Strong written and verbal communication, comfortable working directly with research scientists and interfacing with the customers and frontier labs we partner with.
  • Bonus: responsible-AI considerations for speech, such as bias across accents and dialects and privacy and consent in voice data.

The expected salary range for this position is $160,000 - $185,000 p/year, based on experience, skills, and qualifications.

jobs.description:
About Dropzone AI

Dropzone’s mission is to scale cybersecurity beyond human limits, and augment every single human security engineer/analyst with an army of AI security specialists. Humans alone cannot sufficiently protect our digital future, and AI augmentation is the only way for defenders to reclaim the high ground. We are an award winning company disrupting the $200B+ cybersecurity market.

Powered by Gen AI advancements, our technology offloads repetitive day-to-day work and frees human analysts to focus on real threats and higher-value projects. We are venture-backed, and our team has a rare blend of deep experience across cybersecurity, AI/ML, and SaaS product development. Join us if you want to be on the ground floor of using Gen AI to transform cyber defense. Learn more at.

About the role

We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to own the two squads that decide whether Dropzone works on day one of a deployment and whether it keeps working at scale.

The Integrations squad gets every eligible signal source into the AI SOC Team complete, deduplicated, and once, so no alert goes uninvestigated because of a data gap. The Platform squad makes connecting and administering Dropzone something customers do themselves, including tenant management for MSSPs, access control, audit trail, case management, and governed response actions.

These squads share one outcome: the time from contract signature to trusted, self-serve coverage of a customer's full signal estate. Today that number depends too heavily on our sales engineers and support team. Your job is to make it a product number.

This is a senior individual contributor role embedded in product/engineering trios. You own the customer problem, the business outcome, prioritization, and the honest answer to whether we succeeded. You will not be handed a roadmap. You'll help discover the problem, define the right solution, and own whether it lands. You'll report to the Head of Product.

What you'll do

  • Serve as product lead in two cross-functional trios alongside engineering and design, owning the customer problem, business outcome, and prioritization for each squad.
  • Lead continuous discovery with SOC analysts, SOC managers, MSSP operators, and platform administrators. You talk to customers every week, not every quarter.
  • Define and instrument the metrics that tell us, per customer, whether their signal estate is fully covered and whether they got there without our help.
  • Run the integration prioritization process: reconcile requests from sales, POCs, customer success, and production telemetry into a stack-rank that survives contact with a closing deal.
  • Decide which integration categories Dropzone builds, partners for, or declines, and document the reasoning so the company stops re-litigating it.
  • Turn admin, tenant, audit, and access workflows into product that enterprise and MSSP customers configure themselves, with the governance controls regulated buyers require.
  • Own the response action surface with the maturity model we hold ourselves to: recommend, preview, approve, execute, verify, learn. Nothing executes without human-defined authorization and a verifiable trail.
  • Ship in small increments, measure impact, and adjust. Every release carries the problem it solves, the outcome it supports, a metric to watch, and a named validation owner.
  • Contribute to the product operating model: help define what good discovery, prioritization, and release look like at Dropzone.

Requirements

  • 6+ years of product management experience, with at least 2 years owning platform, integrations, or infrastructure-adjacent product where the customer is technical and the failure modes are quiet.
  • Experience shipping in security, observability, data infrastructure, or an adjacent domain. You can hold your own with a SOC analyst on how an alert moves from an EDR or SIEM into a case.
  • A demonstrated discovery practice. You can describe the last assumption you were wrong about and how you found out before you shipped it.
  • A track record of outcome-based roadmaps: decisions that changed measurable customer behavior, not feature lists that got approved.
  • Comfort being the person who says no to a customer request and can explain why in language the account executive can repeat.
  • Strong written communication. Most of your influence here happens in documents read by people who were not in the meeting.
  • The habit of separating facts from inferences in your own work, and noticing when others do not.
  • A preference for focused ownership over distributed coordination. You do your best work deeply embedded in a problem with a small, accountable team.

Preferred

  • Cybersecurity or security operations domain experience.
  • Experience with MSSP, multi-tenant, or regulated deployment models.
  • Experience at Series A–C stage companies with small, fast-moving product teams.
  • Familiarity with continuous discovery, JTBD, and outcome-oriented product operating models. If Inspired and The Lean Product Playbook describe how you already work, you will feel at home here.
  • Hands-on fluency with data and telemetry tooling, or code-based prototyping.

Work Environment/Travel

We are a 100% remote company where you will work from your home with company-provided equipment to set you up for success. Semi-frequent travel to professional office settings and other events locally and nationally; some overnight travel expected.

Compensation

In the spirit of pay transparency, we are excited to share the base salary range below, exclusive of fringe benefits or potential bonuses. If you are hired at Dropzone your final base salary compensation will be determined based on factors such as geographic location, skills, education, and/or experience. In addition, all compensation packages include significant above market new hire equity grants because we believe in rewarding long term value creation. If you are hired at Dropzone your final base salary compensation will be determined based on factors such as geographic location, skills, education, and/or experience. In addition to those factors, we believe in the importance of pay equity and consider internal equity of our current team members as a part of any final offer. Please keep in mind that hiring at the maximum of the range would not be typical to allow for future and continued salary growth. We also offer a generous benefits package, including company paid health insurance, 401K Plan with employer match, Self-Managed PTO, parental leave, and more.

$175,000—$190,000 USD

At Lumen, you’ll work on infrastructure customers rely on today and build for what’s next, where performance, security, and resilience matter.

The work is challenging, expectations are clear, and trust is built into how we operate. If you’re ready to take ownership, deliver meaningful impact, and help shape the future of AI‑ready connectivity, join us today.

The Role

Identifies and develops new Large Enterprise sales opportunities, provides product solutions, ensures customer satisfaction, and maintains positive ongoing relationships to maximize sales for the company. Introduces company products and services to new and/or existing customers. Responsible for the implementation of strategic and tactical sales account plans. Develops and maintains accurate sales and/or revenue forecasts and management of quota funnels.

Location

jobs.description:
Focused on employment and labor law since 1958, Jackson Lewis P.C.’s 1,000+ attorneys located in major cities nationwide consistently identify and respond to new ways workplace law intersects business. We help employers develop proactive strategies, strong policies and business-oriented solutions to cultivate high-functioning workforces that are engaged and stable, and share our clients’ goals to emphasize belonging and respect for the contributions of every employee.

The Firm is ranked in the First Tier nationally in the category of Labor and Employment Litigation, as well as in both Employment Law and Labor Law on behalf of Management, in the U.S. News - Best Lawyers® “Best Law Firms”.

Job Summary

The Practice Innovation Attorney will play a pivotal role in advancing the firm’s broader innovation objectives by identifying high-value opportunities to improve legal work, translating practice needs into practical technology- and GenAI-enabled solutions, and leading the adoption of new solutions by attorneys and legal professionals. The role will help shape how emerging technologies are evaluated, developed, and incorporated into legal practice in ways that are practical, scalable, responsible, and aligned with firm priorities.

Reporting to the Manager of AI and Innovation, the Practice Innovation Attorney will advise and collaborate with practice group leadership, attorneys, knowledge management professionals, IT, legal engineers, and external vendors to identify opportunities, define requirements, develop and validate solutions, and drive adoption across the firm. The role requires a strong understanding of legal practice, particularly litigation with a preferred focus on Labor & Employment, demonstrated familiarity with legal AI and GenAI tools (e.g., Harvey, Westlaw AI, Lexis+ AI, CoCounsel, or similar platforms), and the ability to translate complex technology capabilities into practical applications for legal professionals.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Practice Discovery and Use-Case Strategy

  • Engage practice leaders, attorneys, and business professionals to identify recurring challenges, inefficiencies, and opportunities for innovation and AI-enabled improvement.
  • Evaluate and prioritize opportunities based on practice value, feasibility, risk, scalability, and alignment with firm priorities.
  • Map current and future-state legal workflows and define practical requirements for selected solutions.
  • Develop recommendations for how GenAI and other emerging technologies can improve legal workflows, client service, and the delivery of legal services.

Solution Design and Validation

  • Translate legal and business requirements into clear use cases, workflows, and functional requirements.
  • Partner with legal engineers, knowledge management, IT, and vendors to develop, test, and refine solutions.
  • Design and conduct legal workflow testing, including output review, issue identification, and documentation of appropriate use and limitations.
  • Help develop safeguards, guidance, and escalation paths for responsible use of AI and other emerging technologies.

Adoption and Practice Engagement

  • Lead adoption efforts for assigned tools and use cases, including demonstrations, targeted training, coaching, communications, and workflow integration.
  • Collaborate with HR Learning and Professional Development teams to integrate innovation and AI initiatives into onboarding, attorney development, and ongoing learning programs.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor to practice leaders and knowledge management on the responsible and effective use of firm-approved AI and GenAI tools.
  • Develop practical playbooks, prompt guidance, examples, and quick-reference resources to facilitate effective use and adoption.
  • Establish feedback channels and use adoption and user feedback data to improve solutions, workflows, and user experience.

Market Awareness and Continuous Improvement

  • Monitor legal AI capabilities, developments in professional responsibility guidance, and relevant changes in legal service delivery.
  • Assess new platform features and recommend whether and how they should be introduced into firm workflows.
  • Share lessons learned and reusable approaches through the Innovation Center of Excellence and other appropriate firm forums.
  • Identify emerging opportunities and advise firm leadership on trends, capabilities, and potential applications that advance firmwide innovation objectives.

Required Qualifications

  • Juris Doctor (JD) from an accredited law school.
  • Minimum of 5 years of legal practice experience or equivalent experience in legal technology, legal operations, or legal innovation roles.
  • Demonstrated experience with legal AI and GenAI platforms (e.g., Harvey, Westlaw AI, Lexis+ AI, CoCounsel, or similar tools).
  • Strong understanding of legal workflows, litigation processes, and how emerging technologies can be applied to common legal tasks.
  • Demonstrated ability to identify opportunities, develop practical recommendations, and lead cross-functional initiatives from concept through adoption.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to advise and influence diverse audiences and translate complex technical concepts into practical guidance.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively across departments and practice groups, with strong judgment and project leadership skills.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Background in labor and employment law or litigation practice.
  • Experience with change management or technology adoption initiatives in a law firm or professional services environment.
  • Familiarity with eDiscovery platforms, document management systems, and legal research databases.
  • Prior experience working with legal innovation or practice technology teams.
  • Experience leading cross-functional technology, process improvement, or AI adoption initiatives.

Competencies & Skills

  • Innovation & Strategic Thinking: Ability to identify high-value opportunities, assess emerging capabilities, and connect technology initiatives to firmwide priorities and legal practice needs.
  • Legal Technology & GenAI Fluency: Deep familiarity with the legal AI ecosystem and an understanding of how GenAI and other technologies can be integrated into legal workflows and practice management systems.
  • Solution Design & Execution: Ability to translate practice needs into clear use cases, requirements, workflows, and practical solutions, and to drive initiatives through validation and adoption.
  • Advisory & Influence: Trusted advisor who can engage senior stakeholders, communicate recommendations clearly, and build alignment across practice groups and business functions.
  • Communication & Presentation: Exceptional ability to communicate complex technology concepts in plain language and effectively demonstrate tools and use cases to legal professionals.
  • Judgment & Risk Awareness: Strong judgment regarding responsible AI use, legal ethics, information governance, and appropriate safeguards and escalation paths.
  • Collaboration & Relationship Building: Proven ability to work cross-functionally with attorneys, IT, leadership, legal engineers, and vendors to achieve strategic goals.

Reporting Structure & Work Arrangement

This position reports under the AI and Innovation Group. The Practice Innovation Attorney will work closely with practice group leaders, knowledge management attorneys, IT, legal engineers, and firm leadership on a day-to-day basis.

This role may require occasional travel to firm offices for in-person demonstrations, targeted training, or other innovation initiatives and is eligible for a hybrid or remote work arrangement in accordance with firm policy.

jobs.description:
About Us:

Our purpose is to help clients exceed their financial health goals. Across the reimbursement cycle, our scalable solutions and clinical expertise help solve programmatic needs. Enabling our teams with leading technology allows analytics to guide our solutions and keeps us accountable achieving goals.

We build long-term careers by investing in YOU. We seek to create an environment that cultivates your professional development and personal growth, as we believe your success is our success.

JOB SUMMARY:

About the Role The Database Engineering team owns the data infrastructure behind CorroHealth's Utilization Management (UM) and Clinical Documentation Improvement (CDI) lines of business. That includes the ETL pipelines, integrations and databases that every downstream analytics product depends on. As a Database Engineer, you'll build and support mission-critical pipelines processing data on sometimes rapid frequencies. You'll work with operations and clinical stakeholders to turn business needs into reliable, well-documented data solutions. You'll report to the Director of Database Development & Operations and join a small team of experienced engineers.

This is remote position.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:
Note: The essential duties and responsibilities below are intended to describe the general duties and responsibilities of this position and are not intended to be an exhaustive statement of duties. This position may perform all or most of the primary duties listed below. Specific tasks, responsibilities or competencies may be documented in the Team Member’s performance objectives as outlined by the Team Member’s immediate Leadership Team Member.

Sadly, we are on high alert for scams, imposters and application fraud.

We employ comprehensive screening and verification methods. Any attempt at application fraud or misrepresentation will be identified and lead to immediate removal from consideration.


Permanent Work Status Required (USC or GC)


Employees must reside and work within the continental U.S.

This is a remote position.

What You'll Do

  • Build and maintain ETL pipelines: design, build and support data pipelines using T-SQL stored procedures, PowerShell and Python, orchestrated through JAMS and SQL Agent.
  • Work on integrations: develop and support bidirectional Salesforce ↔ SQL Server sync (Relational Junction, DBAmp) and secure file-based integrations (SFTP / GoAnywhere MFT) with clients and partners.
  • Design databases: create and evolve schemas, views, stored procedures and indexing strategies that scale with the business.
  • Tune performance: diagnose and fix slow queries and jobs using execution plans, Query Store, wait statistics and index analysis.
  • Ensure data quality: build validation and reconciliation checks so data stays accurate from source to report. Investigate and resolve discrepancies when they come up.
  • Build reporting: develop and maintain SSRS reports and Power BI datasets that support operations and decision-making.
  • Protect PHI: build solutions that meet HIPAA requirements, including least-privilege access, secure transfer and auditability.
  • Support production: monitor scheduled jobs, troubleshoot failures and drive root-cause fixes. Take part in on-call rotation for after-hours monitoring of critical jobs.
  • Follow engineering practices: use source control (Azure DevOps Git repositories), take part in code review, and follow change-management processes for production deployments.
  • Document your work: write and maintain technical documentation and runbooks, and help capture undocumented process knowledge.
  • Collaborate: work with operations leaders, analysts and clinical teams to clarify requirements and explain technical tradeoffs in plain language.

What You Bring

  • 3+ years of hands-on T-SQL development on Microsoft SQL Server
  • Strong command of stored procedures, query tuning, indexing and data modeling
  • Experience building and supporting production ETL processes, including scheduling, error handling and restartability
  • Scripting experience in PowerShell and/or Python for automation and integration
  • Experience working with healthcare data and an understanding of HIPAA obligations for PHI
  • Experience with SSRS and/or Power BI
  • Comfort with source control and working in a code-review culture
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems or a related field, or equivalent practical experience

Nice to Have

  • Utilization management, clinical review, CDI, claims, denials or appeals data
  • Salesforce data integration (DBAmp, Relational Junction or similar)
  • JAMS or another enterprise job scheduler
  • Azure data services
  • Managed file transfer (GoAnywhere or similar)

How You Work

  • You chase a data discrepancy until you find its root cause, not just its symptom.
  • You can explain a pipeline failure to a non-technical operations lead and agree with them on next steps.
  • You document as you build, because you know someone else will support it at 2 a.m.
  • You manage competing priorities across several stakeholders without letting production quality slip.

We Offer

  • Quality of life with a remote predictable, full-time schedule
  • Competitive Salary commensurate to experience
  • Medical, Dental, Vision coverage and more
  • Long-term disability insurance, and life insurance
  • Ample parental leave
  • 401K with company match
  • Certification and Tuition Reimbursement
  • Holidays, Flexible Time Off

PHYSICAL DEMANDS:
Note: Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions as described. Regular eye-hand coordination and manual dexterity is required to operate office equipment. The ability to perform work at a computer terminal for 6-8 hours a day and function in an environment with constant interruptions is required. At times, Team Members are subject to sitting for prolonged periods. Infrequently, Team Member must be able to lift and move material weighing up to 20 lbs.
